Parts P118 / P119 carry the chain-ii specification; the EEPROM copy means a missing or corrupt card can never lose the mileage (luxury F-007 gains that clause).

title: The ICU lives in a protected enclosure with its connector halves built…
body: **D-270 — The ICU lives in a protected enclosure with its connector halves built into the wall: two Deutsch DT13 flanged PCB receptacles (6-way power / bus, 12-way sensors) on the board, sealed through one face; the display ribbon and the page button through grommets in the opposite face; an RF-transparent wall in front of the radio's antenna. The harness side of `DP-ICU-A` / `DP-ICU-B` becomes a DT06 plug on a 150 mm tail from the dash post, so the ICU plugs in like any bought module. The enclosure is 3D-printed in ASA or PETG (never PLA — a dash reaches 70 °C in the sun) around the board, with printed bosses for the DT13 flanges and a gasket groove in the lid; a polycarbonate Hammond 1554-series box is the fallback if printing disappoints.** Camden's call, 2026-09-08, answering `Q-126`: "keep the ICU in a protected container … ideally the connectors are embedded and the harness just plugs in like any other bought part" — and his question, one connector like the PMU or two: **two**, because the whole harness is already tooled for DT (a single 18-way would mean an HD30 / DRC family, new contacts, new tools, a bigger flange), because the 6-way is the module pattern every drop shares (D-252) and the 12-way keeps sensors on their own housing, and because "out" is only the display — CAN is on the 6-way both ways, so nothing else leaves the box. Consequences: `DP-ICU-A` / `DP-ICU-B` box_side become DT13-06PA / DT13-12PA (P122); the two DT04 receptacle kits leave the Deutsch count (P099, P115 re-drawn) and the two post clips with them (P030 → 21); `V-073`'s edge rule (D-265) is the enclosure's face rule. Printing is at CSU's makerspace if it has one, else any print service — the file is ours either way.

title: The ICU carrier's parts check (`V-082`) is done: five values change…
body: **D-273 — The ICU carrier's parts check (`V-082`) is done: five values change, the rest stand.** Agent, 2026-09-08, against the datasheets, as `V-082` asked (D-265). **Changes:** (1) the logic buck is an **LMR36015-Q1-class part (60 V in, 1.5 A)** — the LMR33630's 36 V absolute maximum sits under the SMBJ33A's ~53 V clamping voltage, so a load dump the clamp lets through would take the buck; (2) the backlight switch is a **≥ 60 V device** for the same reason — an SQD50P06-class P-FET or a VN5E-class high-side driver rated ≥ 6 A — behind a **4 A fuse**, because the 900–1000-nit bar and its scaler draw ~2.5 A at 12 V (D-269), not the 2 A the 3 A fuse assumed; (3) the **LM393 runs from 5 V** with 10 kΩ pull-ups to 3V3 — its common-mode input range stops 1.5 V below its supply, so on 3.3 V the tach stage's 5.1 V zener node would clip; (4) the IMU is an **LSM6DSO or ICM-42688-P** — the MPU-6050 and ICM-20948 are not recommended for new designs; (5) the ESP32-C3 sits on **its own 3.3 V LDO** (the XIAO module's) — a BLE scan peaks near 300 mA and the Teensy's regulator is a 250 mA part. **Confirmed as drawn:** SS34 and SMBJ33A at each 12 V input, the BAT54S clamps, BZX84C5V1, the 100 Ω 1 W excitations (D-260), the 15 kΩ / 10 kΩ and 47 kΩ / 10 kΩ dividers, TCAN1042HVDRQ1 (D-265), APS6404L-3SQR PSRAM, the DT13-06PA / -12PA receptacles (D-270; the flange-gasket suffix is confirmed at order). The 5 V rail budget is ~0.8 A peak. The same buck finding applies to the DCU's two bucks (luxury `LP08`, `V-083`). Data: `P105`, `P107`, `P109`, `P116`; `IC04`, `IC12`, `IC13`, `IC23`, `IC24`; `ICU-CARRIER.md`. Closes `V-082`.

title: Reserves live at the post, never in the engine bay. The engine leg…
body: **D-271 — Reserves live at the post, never in the engine bay. The engine leg carries only what the 12A on the mounts needs plus the CAN2 terminator drop; every future-engine provision is pinned on the PMU side of the L1 receptacles and sealed on the leg side. A new cavity state, RESERVED, says exactly that: `L1-P 2` / `L1-P 3` (O13 / O14, 12 AWG from the pins to the receptacle cavities), `L1-S2 9` (the spare block-B position wired to its cavity, no fuse) and `L1-S2 11` (wired across the node to the ICU's spare input `DP-ICU-B 9`) are RESERVED; `L1-S2 4 · 5 · 6` become sealing plugs — a sensor spare with no destination at the post is pinned at the swap, when it has one. The same rule for the chassis legs: a branch with no device ends at the last connector of the main leg, not at a capped wire near where a device might one day be (`Q-132` applies it to the three existing stubs).** Camden's call, 2026-09-08, answering `Q-127` in his own words: "wire the PMU, ICU and DCU all in one go, supporting any engine … the chassis legs go fully wired, but branches with no end are just a connector and the main leg; the engine leg is the unique one — completely clean for the current 12A, connecting to the PMU side via a connector with many unpinned spots, so the PMU side can be fully pinned for as many engines and transmissions as possible, but I don't have to wire them past the PMU / fuses / relays." This is D-211(d) made precise: the interface to any future engine is the L1 receptacles at the dash post, pinned; the leg itself is disposable. What leaves the carts: about 110 ft of wire and eight leg-side contacts; what joins: one sealing plug per RESERVED cavity on the leg side (the size-12 and size-16 plug lines are re-counted). `tools/rx7.py` learned the state: the cut list prints a RESERVED cavity as "no leg conductor", the sealing-plug counts take one half per RESERVED cavity, and a pin's destinations read "reserved at the post". *Supersedes* D-007's "capped at the bulkhead" for O13 / O14 and the three sensor spares, and D-250's leg-side conductors for `L1-S2 9` and `11`; D-252's tunnel pair `L4-S 3 / 4` is untouched — it is a chassis leg and now has a device (`Q-309`).

title: Road speed is a Hall pulse generator on the transmission's speedo-drive…
body: **D-272 — Road speed is a Hall pulse generator on the transmission's speedo-drive boss, the cable deleted; the tunnel pair goes LIVE at the meters cutover.** Camden, 2026-09-08, on `Q-309`: "Follow recommendations assuming many transmissions will be able to support the same type of system even if a different sensor at the trans is needed. but if the transmission base dies when the jatco trans does its not the path." The condition holds: the sensor is a bought part on a standard speedo-drive thread, so the same kind of sensor fits whatever transmission follows the Jatco if it has a drive, and if it has none (the CD009) speed arrives on the same ICU channel from the ECU's VSS frame (engine-swap HO15, luxury F-014) — the approach outlives this transmission either way. Data: `L4-S 3` (signal) and `L4-S 4` (supply) are LIVE; the supply is an O10 tap (N70) so the sensor lives and dies with the ICU, and the block-B spare position stays the phase-2 sensor supply for `L1-S2 9` alone (N68); `DP-ICU-B 8` LIVE, `IC08`; `DV47`, `G35`; `P113` re-specified (Dakota Digital SEN-01-4160 / AutoMeter 5291 class, 8 000 or 16 000 pulses per mile), bought after M-2 measures the boss; MG22 carries it. Pulses per mile is a config value, trued once against a measured mile. Closes `Q-309`; the pending audit's `Q-115` (road speed) is answered by this.

title: The chassis principle: a future circuit's conductor ends in a…
body: **D-274 — The chassis principle: a future circuit's conductor ends in a dust-capped receptacle at the point it leaves its leg, never as a capped wire where the device will be; the two release solenoids are the exception because they exist, and are wired to; the door receptacles are RESERVED at the sill.** Camden, 2026-09-08, on `Q-132`: "wire both release solenoids all the way to the part. both solenoids actual exist and i believe work. the heated wiper spray will no be run all the way to the part just into the front chassis leg and into half of a connector pair, then i run the rest and plug in when the part is here. verify that other chasis future circuits follow the same principle (ends at a connector at the branch off each main leg)." The verification: seven provisions ran past their branch point as bare capped wire; each now ends in a receptacle there, the `L3-BLW` pattern (D-253), and the plug half of each pair waits on the shelf for the part. **`L2-NZL`** (DT-2, cowl) for the nozzle feed `L2-S 6`; **`L2-OAT`** (DT-2, nose) for the outside-air thermistor `L2-S 5`; **`L3-CMF`** (DTP-2, behind the centre stack) for the O15 comfort bus `L3-P 2` — the luxury package's fuse block plugs in; **`L3-WIN`** (DT-6, console) for the four window commands `L3-S2 3–6` plus a switch-common feed tapped off the F3 switch supply where `L3-S2 2` passes; **`L3-MOD`** (DT-2, behind the dash) for the future module `L3-S2 7 / 8`; **`L3-RDR`** and **`L4-RDR`** (DT-4, behind the dash and at the rear node) for the radar pass-through `L3-S3 1–3` ↔ `L4-S 5–7` — the run up the hatch goes in with the sensor. The window commands `L4-M 9–12` already end at the sill node's relay sockets, which is their branch point. **The doors:** the door harness is the mirror's and the window's job, so `D1` / `D2` are RESERVED (D-271's state) — pinned on the node side at the sill, sealing plugs in the door plugs; nothing crosses a hinge boot until there is a part on the other side. **The solenoids:** `L4-M 3` runs through the hinge loop to the hatch-release solenoid and `L4-M 4` to the fuel-door solenoid — both factory parts, present and believed working (K-017 said the fuel-door one never existed; corrected) — their post ends capped until the luxury package fits the trigger (D-180: the K3 / K4 sockets are the slot). **The engine bay is untouched:** the L1 leg's reserves are D-271's, at the post. Data: seven housings and twenty-two cavities (ten of them plugs), fourteen door cavities RESERVED, `DV48` / `DV49`, parts `P030` (28 clips), `P035`, `P036`, `P099`, `P100`, `P102`, `P028` / `P029` (the plug counts), new `P123`–`P125`; `views.py` — the new housing codes join the cut-list groups and the cavity-reference patterns, and the dangling-reference check now also reads the two-letter drop suffixes (`DP-ICU-A n`). Luxury D-315 mirrors it. Closes `Q-132`.

title: The digital display is this build's, installed with the ICU: there is…
body: **D-268 — The digital display is this build's, installed with the ICU: there is no temporary cluster, no CLU pigtail and no gauge drive. The factory cluster stays alive on the factory harness until the meters cutover (MG22), which is gated on the display proven on the bench, and leaves with that harness at install §6. The display chain — the BT817 evaluation board (`T-051`), the glass (`V-085`), the timings (`V-084`) and parts P117–P120 — moves into this project; road speed (`Q-309`) is fitted at the cutover; the odometer starts from the factory cluster's reading and persists to microSD (luxury F-007, a cutover gate); the display mounts on a plain plate in the binnacle aperture (P121) and the moulded bezel around it is the luxury package's (luxury FT34, D-314).** Camden's call, 2026-09-07, answering `Q-129`: install the display now and leave only the dash plastics — a foam-and-fibreglass mould around the display — to the luxury package; wiring for one instrument is cleaner than wiring for two. The reason it costs nothing in safety is one the design already had: the parallel-system migration (D-023 / D-024) keeps the factory cluster on the factory harness until its own circuit's cutover, so the fallback D-258 built a pigtail for exists without a wire. What leaves the record: `DV32`, channels IC17–IC20, the CLU header, install §1.22–1.23 as they were, the cluster letters of T-017 sheet C, and D-263 — withdrawn as moot, the gauges' construction no longer matters. What it pulls forward: the display chain's bench work (weeks, in parallel with a harness build that takes months), a pulse generator before the first drive without the cluster, and persistence for the odometer. *Amends* D-258 (the cluster's temporary role and everything built for it; the topology — senders terminate at the ICU, no cluster drop, the PMU-excited oil node — stands) and D-259 ("only the display comes with luxury" → only the bezel does).

title: The ICU carries a radio co-processor: an ESP32-C3 module on the…
body: **D-267 — The ICU carries a radio co-processor: an ESP32-C3 module on the carrier's 3.3 V rail, on a UART to the Teensy, decoding battery data over Bluetooth LE and republishing it as a CAN frame (`0x220`, 2 Hz — volts, amps, state of charge, temperature, flags) that the display draws and the PMU logs. Nothing at the drops or in the harness changes; the enclosure wall in front of its antenna must be RF-transparent, or the antenna goes outside (a constraint on `Q-126`). A dev board is bought now to try the decode (`P116`); which source it decodes — the Ionic's BMS, a shunt, or both — is `Q-128`.** Camden's call, 2026-09-07: "the board is cheap and worth buying to try; if it is an isolated addition inside the ICU case leaving everything the same, then definitely plan to add it." It is: channel `IC24`, two UART lines and two GPIOs on the board, ~120 mA on a rail budgeted at 0.6 A, no cavity, no conductor, no cart line beyond the module. The Teensy stays the ICU's brain (the reasoning is in Q-128: the ESP32's ADC, its render bandwidth, the Teensy-shaped firmware, three Teensys in hand); the radio's boot time and its FreeRTOS timing never touch the instrument core. Because the ICU's logic rail is O10 (accessory), the radio runs only with the key in — the overnight consumption is read at key-on from the BMS's or the shunt's own counters, which is what G4 needs. D-251 holds: the frame is telemetry; state of charge may enter the 11.5 V shed rule only as a secondary, fail-open term. The frame's layout is the luxury CAN map's (`0x220`); the firmware work is luxury `F-015`.

title: The sensor inputs are built to outlive the 12A. Every ICU sender…
body: **D-262 — The sensor inputs are built to outlive the 12A. Every ICU sender channel is a pull-up behind a jumper (fitted for the 12A's 2-wire resistive senders, open for a 0–5 V transducer), a ×0.4 divider that reads either, and a per-channel curve in config-as-data — never a board change; the PMU's A7 takes a resistive sender with the 100 Ω pull-up in (D-260) or a 0–5 V pressure transducer with it lifted at `N39`; the engine leg is cut at the grommet and rebuilt at the swap (D-211(d)), and what the new engine must deliver to these inputs is the hand-over table in `../engine-swap/README.md`.** Camden, 2026-09-07: "with the engine swap I will need to power the more complicated sensors" — and the bay stays stripped, so nothing is pre-wired for a sensor that does not exist. The 12A's senders are one-wire resistive parts the ICU excites; an LS's are 3-wire 5 V devices read by its own ECU, which publishes them on CAN2 (`0x500+`, the luxury map). So at the swap most ICU channels go quiet and the display reads the ECU's frames — a firmware rule, luxury `F-014`: local input when configured, else the ECU's frame, else dashes (luxury D-153) — while the two signals the *car* acts on stay on wire per D-251: oil pressure into A7 from a sender or transducer on the new block (never the ECU's CAN value), and the tach into `DP-ICU-B 4` from the ECU's tach output through the same clamp. `L1-S2 9` (switched 12 V, D-250) powers a 12 V-supplied 3-wire transducer if one is fitted; a 5 V sensor is the ECU's, or gets a regulator at the dash node — no +5 V goes down the leg (D-215). The three reserves `L1-S2 4–6` and the spare `L1-S2 11 → DP-ICU-B 9` are the only new-sensor conductors, and they already exist.

title: The 12A's electrical sensors are the three senders and nothing else.…
body: **D-264 — The 12A's electrical sensors are the three senders and nothing else. The cut B-12 water-temperature switch stays in the thermostat housing as the port's plug, unconnected; the oil level float switch (C-06) is not wired and the CLU pigtail stays at twelve lines; there is no oil-temperature sender on the 12A and no conductor is run for one — `L1-S2 10` and `DP-ICU-B 7` become sealing plugs, `N65` and `P112` leave the record, and the ICU keeps the IC07 footprint for the swap.** Camden's three answers, 2026-09-07: `Q-124` "verified unneeded — leave it as the plug, unconnected"; `Q-125` "no need for the added warning light — I check the oil every time I get gas"; `Q-308` "no oil-temp sensor while the 12A is there; prepare for after the swap, but run no unneeded wire to the engine bay". The last restates the engine-bay rule (D-211(d)) and it wins over D-250's oil-temperature conductor: the leg is rebuilt at the swap anyway, so a wire run now for a sender that will arrive with a different engine serves nothing. What the swap needs is at the dash node — a cavity (`DP-ICU-B 7`, plugged) and a channel (IC07, footprint) — and both stay. Whether the *rest* of L1's reserves follow is `Q-127`. *Supersedes* D-250's oil-temperature conductor (its sensor supply `L1-S2 9` and spare `L1-S2 11` stand until Q-127) and the A-010 clause that left the level senders as a future item — they are out.

title: The gauge rule is set by the enable-at limit, not the channel's rating
body: **D-232 — The gauge rule is set by the enable-at limit, not the channel's rating.** 2026-09-03, a clarification the automated check forced: `DESIGN.md` §13 said "12 AWG on 25 A, 14 AWG on 15 A", and four rows already broke it on purpose — the 16 AWG high-beam-indicator tap on O3 and the three 16 AWG capped module drops on O10. A wire has to survive what its protection lets through, and the protection is the software limit: 12 AWG above 15 A, 14 AWG above 13 A, 16 AWG at 13 A and below. A 16 AWG tap off a heavier feed is allowed only where the cavity notes it as a tap, and the check flags any other case. No wire changes.

title: The factory ignition noise-suppression condenser is reproduced on the…
body: **D-281 — The factory ignition noise-suppression condenser is reproduced on the O12 branch at the coil bracket (P135).** From the 2026-09-08 benchmark; written on the 2026-09-08f repair (the 2026-09-08 script meant to add the part as P099, a number the Deutsch kits already held, so no part existed until now). The 1982 diagram carries a condenser (B-22) on the igniter and coil `BW` supply. Mazda fitted it because the leading and trailing igniters put measurable hash on the ignition bus — and this harness runs CAN2 and eight analog resistor ladders past those coils, which the factory one did not. Fit it on the `L1-P 1` branch at the coil bracket (install 3.7), or delete it only against a measurement showing it is unnecessary. Deleting it silently is the fault that gets misdiagnosed as a bad ladder six months later.

title: Family-colour solid wire, identified by printed labels; no tracers
body: **D-212 — Family-colour solid wire, identified by printed labels; no tracers.** Camden's call, 2026-09-02, after the striped-tracer scheme proved unpurchasable as cut lengths. The colour names the family (RED power · ORN 15 A outputs at 14 AWG · BLK ground · GRY analog inputs · BLU commands · PNK switch supply and +5 V · YEL/GRN CAN); the label at each end names the wire; the cavity number and the design tables are the record. Wire comes as four 16 AWG Prysmian GXL spools from Waytek (black, red, grey, blue) plus 14/12/10 AWG cuts from WireBarn and three short 16 AWG colours (pink, yellow, green). Labels are printed on a Brother PT-D220 onto TZe-FX231 flexible-ID tape, wrapped on the wire, with clear heat-shrink over them where they live under loom or in the engine bay — chosen over heat-shrink-sleeve printers as a quarter of the cost with the same permanence. Supersedes D-016 (base colour = class, tracer = circuit), D-203(c) (PT-E300 + HSe sleeves) and D-203(h) (striped GXL by the foot).

title: SICMA terminal spares come from the two spare 39-way housings in hand…
body: **D-135 / D-220 — SICMA terminal spares come from the two spare 39-way housings in hand (54 small, 32 large), so there is no Ballenger order.** Zero spares in the car's own set is why the practice crimps use the spare sets first.

title: The 2026-09-02 order changes, Camden's own edits to the carts
body: **D-220 — The 2026-09-02 order changes, Camden's own edits to the carts:** the wink switches are the DMWD 1NO+1NC momentary 2-pack (replacing a 5-pack); the ATC fuse assortment is out — the drawer is checked and any missing value bought locally; the 12 × 24 aluminium sheet is out (D-214); a stainless star-washer kit and three clear heat-shrink packs are in; relays are bought without spares; no spare housing pairs.

title: No bench kit: no bench PSU, no plywood mule, no test pigtail
body: **D-141 / D-144 / D-147 — No bench kit: no bench PSU, no plywood mule, no test pigtail.** Every risk the bench was justified by is already covered by the parallel-system architecture (D-023) and the in-car config sequence (D-194).

title: Ground studs are 3/8 stainless with star washers (four: rear, front…
body: **D-205 — Ground studs are 3/8 stainless with star washers (four: rear, front, dash, sill); the PMU stands off its panel on three M6 spacers; F2 (2 A), F19 (3 A) and F15 (7.5 A) are values cheap assortments skip — buy them by value.**

title: Parallel-system migration, least to most consequential, ending with…
body: **D-023 / D-024 — Parallel-system migration, least to most consequential, ending with ignition and start.** The factory harness stays intact and powered until each circuit's own cutover; never both systems on one load; the car drives home at the end of every session.

title: Soft fuses are set from current measured live in the client during…
body: **D-025 / D-174 — Soft fuses are set from current measured live in the client during migration, never from an estimate; the PMU's telemetry on the new harness is the measurement, and its gap against healthy-expected draw is also the list of tired parts to replace afterwards.**

body: **D-176 — Part replacement (a slow wiper motor, a weak pump) is a separate job after the PMU is in, identified from telemetry — not clutter inside the wiring project.**

title: The pop-up motor pinout comes from factory sheet E (E-03 / E-04: YG top…
body: **D-177 / D-199 — The pop-up motor pinout comes from factory sheet E (E-03 / E-04: YG top · WR left · RY right · R bottom; YG is the cam-driven transit contact the ladders read; WR is the constant feed and is capped). Which of R / RY carries the run winding through the cam — bridged or single — is decided by the ohm check at the motor (install M-3), the one measurement the pin plan waits on.**

title: The deliberate soft-fuse trip is a required step, done in the car on…
body: **D-143 / D-145 — The deliberate soft-fuse trip is a required step, done in the car on the first migrated circuit (the interior lamp): set the limit to 2 A, short the output, watch it trip and retry.** It is the single behaviour that distinguishes this device from a fuse box and it must be met on purpose, not at speed.

title: Powered verification of the dash node is replaced by continuity…
body: **D-146 — Powered verification of the dash node is replaced by continuity testing, which needs no power and catches a wrong cavity, a missed crimp, a swapped pair and a short to the panel.** Powered checks happen in the car with every output disabled.

title: Housekeeping that stands: verify the two spare housings' terminal…
body: **D-127 / D-137 / D-103 — Housekeeping that stands: verify the two spare housings' terminal counts on arrival; mark cavity 1 on the housing with the paint pen before the first terminal goes in (D-139); measure the pop-up motors and check the transit contacts in one sitting.**

title: Working files are Markdown; IDs are permanent and never reused; a…
body: **D-026 / D-043 — Working files are Markdown; IDs are permanent and never reused; a closed question is cited with its closer.**

title: The record is `data/*.csv`; every document with a table in it is…
body: **D-233 — The record is `data/*.csv`; every document with a table in it is rendered.** Camden's call, 2026-09-03, after the eleven "downstream edits still to make" showed what hand-mirrored tables cost: one fact in one row, referenced by ID everywhere else. `tools/rx7.py` loads the tables, refuses to build on any contradiction (a cavity without a source, a fuse without a load, a ladder window that overlaps, a cart line below the design's count, an unknown ID) and renders `DESIGN.md`, `GLOSSARY.md`, `SHOPPING-LIST.md`, `INSTALL.md`, `WIRE-TABLES.md`, `PMU-CONFIG-SHEET.md`, `README.md` and `VIEW.html` from `templates/` (the prose) and `data/` (the facts). Derived facts — a pin's destinations, a housing's used count, a wire label, the Deutsch kit counts, ADC centres, totals — are computed, never typed. Generated files carry a banner and are never edited by hand; `DECISIONS.md` and `QUESTIONS.md` stay prose. Supersedes D-221 (the tables were the record and the generator was retired — that put the same row in four files) and revives the intent of the 2026-08-30 CSV convention in a shape that keeps the documents readable.

title: The drawing is a view: one master harness sheet, rendered by `build`…
body: **D-275 — The drawing is a view: one master harness sheet, rendered by `build` from the tables with WireViz; the hand-drawn SVGs are retired.** Camden, 2026-09-08: "follow recommendation make a blend prioritizing wireViz for a full harness diagram with all details as the master all in one sheet from battery to part to ground every path every detail … id rather have one big table than many small ones i need to peice together." `harness.py` builds a WireViz description from the same rows as every document — `cavities.src` for each cavity's box side, `devices.terminals` for its device end, `relays` for the terminals no cavity names, `fuses.fed_from` for the inline feeds, `cables.run` for the backbone, `grounds` for the studs — and `tools/rx7.py build` runs it after the checks pass: `01-DESIGN/diagrams/HARNESS.yml` is always written; `HARNESS.svg` and `HARNESS.html` (with the bill of materials) are rendered when Graphviz and wireviz are installed, and a stamp records the data they came from, so `{{harness_status}}` in DESIGN §1 says **STALE** the moment they are not. Housings are drawn as mated pairs with their cavities coloured by state; bundles are grouped by zone and gauge; every wire row names both of its ends. Two conventions the drawing needed and the data did not state: the door window-motor legs are drawn to the K5–K8 sockets' terminal 30 (the SPDT pair's common), and a device line the parser cannot resolve is reported in the build output, never dropped. The twelve hand-drawn SVGs move to `99-ARCHIVE/Electrical/2026-09-08_hand-drawn-diagrams/` (finishing-list A8 closes); whether a second, backbone-only SVG generator is wanted is decided after the sheet has been used. Cost: one script, once — every rebuild is free. `views.py` gains `PRE_BUILD`; `rx7.py` runs it, and no longer scales an inline drawing to the pane.

title: Five sheets are cut from the harness model beside the master: one per…
body: **D-276 — Five sheets are cut from the harness model beside the master: one per leg, beginning to end, and the dash node.** Camden, 2026-09-08: four leg diagrams — rear, dash, front, engine — that start at the leg connector at the PMU / relay / fuse box and end at the parts, with fewer overlapping wires; the rear leg to extend to the dash always-hot busbar with the power backbone to that point. His answers to the four design questions: a leg sheet begins at the leg's post housings with each cavity labelled with what feeds it (no PMU / fuse / relay nodes drawn); the dash node is a fifth sheet of its own; the rear sheet owns everything that starts at the battery or the rear stud (Class-T → busbar, disconnect → rear stud, the 1/0 starter run and the 1/0 cranking return, the sill node) and the engine sheet owns the bay's cables with 'from the battery' stubs; straight-run routing. How: `harness.py` builds one model and `subset()` cuts each sheet by conductor group — `LEG-Lx` and `GND-Lx` for a leg, `DASH-NODE` for the node, backbone cables by id — so a conductor is never typed twice. Bundles are per housing (the housing a leg conductor leaves, the housing a node conductor lands on), which is what took the crossings out: each bundle sits beside its housing and the sheet reads left to right. One deviation from the routing answer: Graphviz's true orthogonal router ignores port positions, so wires would no longer land on their pins — the leg sheets use `polyline` (straight segments with bends) instead; the master and node sheets keep splines because of their density. Outputs: `LEG-L1.svg` … `LEG-L4.svg`, `DASH-NODE.svg`, each with an `.html` twin and its own stamp; `{{harness_status}}` reports all six. DESIGN §6 shows each leg's sheet under its heading and §5.3 the node sheet; INSTALL §2–§4 point at them. Extends D-275.

title: The shopping list is the four live carts of 2026-09-02 — Waytek $455.04…
body: **D-222 — The shopping list is the four live carts of 2026-09-02 — Waytek $455.04 · WireBarn $382.68 · DeutschConnector.com $944.08 · Amazon $1,096.22 — plus the short list of gaps in `02-SHOPPING/SHOPPING-LIST.md` §8.** Nothing has been purchased; every cart waits for Camden's review and payment. Supersedes D-207's cart figures and the old five-store manifest.

title: The cart is dialed to the design as it stands after D-272 / D-273 /…
body: **D-277 — The cart is dialed to the design as it stands after D-272 / D-273 / D-274, and the Deutsch assembly kits are data.** Camden, 2026-09-08: make the cart perfect — everything the current plan needs and nothing it no longer needs, and every future circuit wired into its main leg and ending in half a connector where it diverges, both halves bought, one fitted. The kit lines were the one place the cart was prose ("the cart holds two pairs"); they are now fourteen lines, one per kit SKU, each with the quantity the cart holds and a `kit:<type>` need rule derived from the housing table, so `build` refuses the moment a housing is added or changed without its kit — the same rule the sealing plugs and clips already lived under. Against the housings today: 12-way plugs drop 7 → 6 and receptacles 7 → 5 (D-258, D-270); 8-way 5 → 6 pairs (L4-S2); 6-way plugs 2 → 4 and receptacles 2 → 3; 4-way 2 → 4 pairs; 2-way 1 → 4 pairs; DTP-2 1 → 3 pairs; DTP-4 stays at 3. Checked and confirmed: sealing plugs (84 / 6), clips (28), the 14 AWG contacts (18 of each), dust caps (2 × 6-way, 3 × 4-way, 3 × 2-way, 2 × DTP-2, no 12-way), relays and their ten sockets, the four inlines, the backbone cable, lugs and boots after D-245 / D-246, the three added 16 AWG colours. Corrected: the label tape to four cartridges (about 300 conductors, two ends each — three cartridges was short), the 14 AWG RED note (the door legs are RESERVED; only the four K5–K8 → D1 / D2 wires remain), the ICU enclosure line (printed ASA / PETG, D-270), and a perfboard for the sense stages and bias resistors, which no line carried. The rule itself holds everywhere but one place: `L4-P 3` and `L4-P 4` end at the sill node's F8 / F9 / F14 positions, which have no holders this build — a bare end on the harness. `Q-133` → D-283 ruled the three holders in now, fitted empty. Extends D-222 / D-238; the §8 gap list is derived from these lines and is the whole of what changes at the four stores.

body: **D-283 — The sill node's F8 / F9 / F14 get their sealed inline holders now, fitted empty — every future circuit ends in a holder or half a connector, none bare.** Camden's call, 2026-09-08, answering `Q-133`: "follow recommendations". Reasoning: D-277's rule — a future circuit is wired into its main leg and ends in half a connector where it leaves it, both halves bought, one fitted — held everywhere except the sill node. The window bus `L4-P 3` (12 AWG, O1) and the comfort feed `L4-P 4` (12 AWG, O15) landed on the F8 / F9 / F14 *positions*, which were labelled but had no holders until the windows and mirrors came, so the two conductors ended bare on the sill panel. Now three more of the sealed inline ATC holders already in the Waytek cart (46047, 14 AWG leads — enough for the 20 A window fuses and the 10 A mirror heat) are fitted empty at the sill: each conductor lands in its holder, no fuse means open, and the luxury package drops a fuse in rather than wiring a holder. Cost about $12; no other change. Consequences in the data: `parts` P002 raises 4 → 7 (F8, F9, F14 join F12, F15, F16, F20); `fuses` F8 / F9 / F14 read "holder fitted, no fuse" and stay EMPTY; the notes on `cavities` L4-P 3 / L4-P 4, `node_conductors` N16 / N17, `pins` 27 and `devices` DV43 say holder, not position — the cavity state stays CAPPED (a dead end with no load, which is what the luxury package's provisions count on); the luxury package's LP37 and PV44 / PV45 lose the holders they were to bring. The phrases "no holder" and "positions only" are retired. Extends D-065 (the sill node) and D-274 (the node is the branch's end); refines D-277.

title: The engine leg is built for the FB/FC alternator only; every other alternator is provided for at the fuse/relay/PMU end, never as wire in the bay
body:
**D-316 — The engine leg is built for the FB/FC alternator only; every other alternator is provided for at the fuse/relay/PMU end, never as wire in the bay.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.01`: "prepare only for a FB/FC alternator in the engine leg with no warning light … however the pmu/relay/fuse section should be pinned and wired to work for an alternator id find on most engines … just like every cuircut in the engine leg, the fuse/relay/pmu are fully done and future proof, the engine leg is bare bones."

**What goes in.** The FB is an **LR** system and stays one: `BW` is the R terminal (ignition-switched regulator wake, under 0.5 A) on `L1-S1 2` through O12 → F15, and `WB` is L, the lamp sink. The `'86-88` FC 70 A unit is a bolt-in with the identical two-terminal interface and needs no wiring change, so it is the ceiling — the single narrow V-belt caps realistic output near 70–90 A anyway.

**No warning-lamp resistor is needed, and this closes that question.** The 100 Ω 5 W parallel resistor noted against D-198 was only ever required for an **LS-type** unit, which uses the lamp itself as the excitation path and therefore never starts charging without a bulb or a substitute load. An LR alternator excites on R; the lamp is decorative. Once the ICU replaces the cluster there is no bulb, and nothing about that stops an FB/FC unit charging. The resistor re-enters the design only if an LS-type unit is ever fitted — which, by this decision, means rebuilding the leg anyway.

**What does not go in.** The **S** (sense) and **P** (phase/FR) conductors are **not** run. `L1-S1 5`, `7`, `8` and `12` stay sealing plugs, and L1-S1's final cavity state is settled by that.

**The general rule this fixes, beyond the alternator.** The engine leg carries only what the engine on the mounts needs today. Future capability lives as **unpinned space at the fuse/relay/PMU connector**, which is assembled once and fully populated, never as capped wire in the bay. The bay stays stripped; the leg is rebuilt from scratch at any engine swap (D-211, D-271). This is the engine-leg counterpart of D-274's chassis principle and it governs every engine-side circuit, not just this one.

title: Future circuits run both conductors down the leg and branch only what the fitted part needs; the wiper park sense is the first case
body:
**D-317 — Future circuits run both conductors down the leg and branch only what the fitted part needs; the wiper park sense is the first case.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.02`: "follow recommendations, prepare for both wires through the front leg, however when the wiper branches off solo only the one needed wire continues after the branch to the part, then if I use other wipers I just pull that tiny branch and pin the second wire (all casis/body/intitor shoud follow this patter for future circuts)."

**The rule, for every chassis, body and interior circuit.** The leg carries **both** conductors as far as the branch point. Past the branch, only the conductor the fitted part actually uses continues to the part. The spare stays unpinned at the branch. Changing to a part that needs the other conductor is then a short branch pulled and a second contact pinned — never a leg re-run. This refines D-274, which ended a future circuit in half a connector where it left its leg: D-274 still governs a circuit whose part does not exist yet, and D-317 governs a circuit whose part exists but whose *variant* may change.

**The wiper case.** Replacement two-speed motors sort into five families. The fitted Japanese OE motor brings the cam out as a **dry SPDT**, which is what the A3 ladder assumes and is correct. The commonest universal on the shelf is the **Bosch/SWF/Valeo DIN 72552** family, which self-parks: the cam's common is the **low-brush node**, `53a` wants a permanent +12 and `53e` is the brake throw — reading either would put battery volts and brush spikes onto A3.

**In the data.** `L2-S 4` is promoted from sealing plug to a `WIPER_PARK_RET` conductor, run to the branch and left there. `L2-M 8` is held as the fused park feed for the same reason. The A3 wiper-park leg is specified **clamped and 12 V tolerant** at the resistor sub-assembly, so no replacement motor in any of the five families can damage an input. Two cavities buy the whole replacement population.

title: CAN never leaves the dashboard: no rear node, no engine-bay drop, and every computer including a future ECU is a dash node
body:
**D-318 — CAN never leaves the dashboard: no rear node, no engine-bay drop, and every computer including a future ECU is a dash node.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.04`: "tested with my phone, and it will reliably view the battery telemetry from much farther than the dash … I do want TPMS and suspect the generalized 10-30 feet tpms sensor radio range will be plenty for the receiver to live in the dash … leaving the CAN only at the front. I also do not want the ecu in the engine bay … the ECU will also be a dash node localized with all the other computers and more intricate wiring, then only the small branches travel everywhere. so that being said CAN should only ever stay inside the dashboard out of sight."

**No rear CAN.** The flip condition in the packet was met and he tested it: the Ionic's BLE carries to the cargo bin and past it, so the gateway lives at the dash node and the rear needs no bus. TPMS is wanted and its sensors reach 10–30 ft, so that receiver is a dash node too. **No camera of any kind is ever fitted to this car** — that removes the other rear-node candidate outright.

**No engine-bay CAN.** `L1-S1 9` and `10` were capped in the bay as the LS ECU's drop, with the bus's far-end 120 Ω terminator across them. A future ECU is now a dash node, so that drop has no consumer and is released: both cavities go back to sealing plugs and the terminator moves to the dash node, which becomes a physical end of the bus rather than the middle of it.

**The shape this fixes.** Every computer — ICU, DCU, the TPMS receiver, the BLE gateway, a future engine ECU — sits at the dash node where the intricate wiring already is. Only thin branches leave the dash to reach sensors and loads. CAN is out of sight and out of the weather, and there is no bus stub anywhere that a later change could turn into a reflection problem.

**In the data.** `cavities` `L1-S1 9` and `L1-S1 10` → PLUG. The engine-swap hand-over `HO03` is rewritten. Nothing is run to the rear, so no L4 cavity changes and the carted 120 Ω resistors (P070, ten of them) are unaffected. The PMU's software termination stays as the design has it, with 120 Ω at both physical ends inside the dash.

title: The master disconnect returns to the positive side: one switch at the battery carrying both the PMU leg and the starter leg
body:
**D-319 — The master disconnect returns to the positive side: one switch at the battery carrying both the PMU leg and the starter leg.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.05`: "follow recommendations and switch positive side". Supersedes **D-245**, which put it in the battery negative.

**Why D-245 was wrong.** Its reasoning held as far as it went — with the negative open, a positive-to-chassis fault has no return path — but three arguments were not considered. **(1) Convention:** ABYC E-9.10.c puts the switch in the cranking-motor supply, NHRA requires the positive side verbatim, and NEC 404.2(B) states the general principle that the grounded conductor is not switched. Anyone who works on this car, a first responder included, will expect a positive-side kill. **(2) The negative leg is unfused by definition:** any parallel negative bond — a shunt, a battery-monitor sense lead, the pack's BMS or heater return, a trickle charger left connected — silently becomes the return path for the whole system. **(3)** With the switch open and the engine running, the battery negative post floats at (Vsys − Vbat) above chassis and sits near spike potential during a load dump.

**In the data.** One positive-side switch at the battery carries both branches — the Class-T/PMU leg and the MRBF/starter leg — so opening it genuinely kills the car. Post-to-switch-to-fuses stays in inches, as D-062 demands. `backbone` B1/B5, `cables` C01/C02/C05 and `grounds` G24 return to a positive-side arrangement, reversing D-245's re-draw. Cost: none — the switch is already carted, and cable lengths shift by about a foot. **Which** e-Series switch it is — 9003e, or the 9004e with its alternator-field-disconnect pole — is still open as `00.12`, so P049's SKU is not changed here.

title: The kick-down is reproduced and stays operational
body:
**D-320 — The kick-down is reproduced and stays operational.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.06`: "option A, as i think the switch and solenoid are functioning as expected now in the car (kickdown seams to work) we should incorporate the kick down into the wiring and keep it operational."

The 1982 component list carries a **kick-down switch (B-32)** at the throttle pedal and a **kick-down solenoid (B-33)** on the transmission — two wires, automatic-only. Both are believed working in the car today. The circuit appeared in no cavity, no device row and no decision, and it was **not** on D-097's deliberate-deletion list; without it the transmission will not force a downshift at wide-open throttle. Option (b) — delete it beside D-097 — is rejected, and (c) — run and cap the tunnel conductor and decide later — is unnecessary now that the answer is known.

**In the data.** This needs a dash-local conductor to the pedal box, a tunnel conductor to the transmission, and a feed with its own protection. Those cavity and fuse assignments are agent work (`W-320`) against the free positions in the L3 and L4 housings rather than guesses made here; the tunnel is open once, so the assignment lands before the L4 cut list is fixed. The switch and solenoid become `devices` rows so the record stops treating them as absent.

title: The starter MRBF goes to 250 A, sized to the 1/0 cable it protects
body:
**D-321 — The starter MRBF goes to 250 A, sized to the 1/0 cable it protects.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.08`: "follow recommendations". Supersedes **D-237**, which fixed it at 200 A.

D-237 was correct when the cable was 2 AWG (~210 A). **D-246 then took the cable to 1/0 (285 A) and nobody re-opened the fuse.** A fuse protects the cable, not the load, so at 1/0 a 200 A rating is sized to the load — conservative in the wrong direction — and the Bussmann MRBF curve is unforgiving of a long crank: 200 % (400 A) opens in a maximum of 60 s, 135 % (270 A) in a maximum of 900 s. A hot rotary that cranks long walks up that curve toward a fuse that was never meant to be the limit.

**In the data.** `fuses` MRBF → 250 A, same Blue Sea 5191 holder, about $17. `parts` P052 becomes the 250 A fuse; its exact Blue Sea SKU is marked `confirm` and verified before the Amazon cart is paid — which, under D-323, is not yet. `V-094` still closes the question properly with a clamp meter on the starter cable during a hot start, rather than from published curves.

title: Limp-home is the config file and a USB-to-CAN cable carried in the car plus a one-page written emergency procedure
body:
**D-322 — Limp-home is the config file and a USB-to-CAN cable carried in the car, plus a one-page written emergency procedure.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.09`: "follow recommendation (i cant afford a spare pmu so definitely give my a way to fix small pmu issues on the go or enable limp mode under worse cases)."

No PDM vendor documents a bypass, backup module or manual override; the corpus treats total module failure as accepted risk and the professional mitigation is a spare configured unit. That is a **racing** answer. This is a street-registered car where brake lamps, ignition and fuel pump are all software-defined on one module that is not automotive-qualified and lives in a 44-year-old dash — and option (c), a spare PMU, is explicitly out on cost.

So options **(a) + (b)** together, which cost a cable and an afternoon: the configuration file and a USB-to-CAN cable **live in the car**, so a soft fault — a mis-set soft fuse, a tripped channel, a bad expression — is fixed at the roadside; and a **one-page written emergency procedure** covers the hard case, feeding fuel pump, ignition and brake lamps directly from the busbar to get the car home. The design had none of the three. Recovery from a *single* dead output is separate and already possible (D-282).

**In the data.** The cable becomes a `parts` row. The procedure is agent work (`W-322`) and lands in the install record when the install steps exist; it is written before first power-up, not after.

title: Nothing is bought until the design is complete and Camden understands it; no cart is paid early
body:
**D-323 — Nothing is bought until the design is complete and Camden understands it; no cart is paid early.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.10`: "Rule everything first i do not want to buy anything until the plan is detail for detail flawless and i undersatand like its already physcaly in the car and working perfectly."

This **overrides the packet's own recommendation**, which was to pay Waytek, WireBarn and DeutschConnector immediately and hold only the Amazon cart. The recommendation optimised for lead time; he is optimising for understanding, and understanding is the thing that cannot be bought twice.

**What it means in practice.** `A1` (pay the four carts) is blocked on the design freeze, not on the four packets that were in front of it. No store is paid while any block that changes a line is open, and the long-lead Deutsch order waits with the rest. The comprehension bar is his, not the checker's: the plan reads as though the car is already built and working, or it is not done.

**Why it costs less than it looks.** D-202's one-teardown logic is untouched — everything is still bought in one pass, the pass simply moves later. The four parts that were about to be bought twice (P049's switch under `00.12`, P052's fuse under D-321, the battery-data source under `00.11`) are exactly the ones this prevents. Nothing in the design depends on parts arriving before the freeze.

**In the data.** `work` `A1` → blocked, gate `design freeze`. The phase gate into SOURCING now carries this decision by name, so no future run can read an empty §1 as permission to pay.

title: The heated washer nozzle and the wiper-park de-icer are cancelled; L2-S 6 and the L2-NZL receptacle come out. The outside-air conductor is untouched
body:
**D-329 — The heated washer nozzle and the wiper-park de-icer are cancelled; `L2-S 6` and the `L2-NZL` receptacle come out. The outside-air conductor is untouched.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `01.06`: "change of plans please void the wiper park heater and washer nozzle heater i decided i do not think they are worth it." Supersedes **D-256**.

D-256 put two front-end conductors in for the climate module and this decision keeps one of them. **`L2-S 5` survives exactly as it was**: the outside-air thermistor at the nose, 16 AWG GRY, grounded at the front star, landing on `DP-DCU 2` at the post through the `L2-OAT` receptacle, with `DP-DCU 6` still a plug. There is no automatic climate control in this car and none is planned; the outside reading is for display, and the cluster shows it beside cabin temperature. That half is untouched and is restated here so one standing decision owns both.

**What comes out.** `L2-S 6` — the 16 AWG RED heated-nozzle / park-de-icer feed — is not run, and the `L2-NZL` DT-2 receptacle at the cowl is not fitted. Both cavities of that housing go with it. This was always conditional: D-256 wrote it as "a comfort-bus load the DCU switches, conditional on a nozzle that can be made to fit", and the condition is now declined rather than unmet. Nothing is stranded — the feed never reached a part.

**Consequences in the data.** `cavities` `L2-S 6` → sealing plug; the `L2-NZL` housing and its two cavities are deleted, which drops the DT-2 count in the Deutsch kits automatically, because D-277 derives those counts from the housing table rather than typing them. The luxury package's comfort bus loses two of its seven switched outputs: `SN16` becomes ×5 — seat heat ×2, seat cool ×2, mirror heat — and stage `S4` loses the nozzle and de-icer from its outcome, its prerequisites and its plug list. Both terms go into `retired.csv` in both projects so they cannot return by accident.

**One number to recheck, not to assume.** D-256 added the 50 ft WireBarn cut `P009` because the 16 AWG RED family calculated at roughly 510 ft against a 500 ft spool, and `L2-S 6` was part of that total. Removing it plausibly drops the family back under the spool, which would delete `P009` — but that is a derived figure and it is recomputed from the wire schedule (`W-329`), never by hand here.

title: Battery data comes from the Ionic BMS over BLE; no shunt is bought, and current and state of charge wait on the protocol
body:
**D-330 — Battery data comes from the Ionic BMS over BLE; no shunt is bought, and current and state of charge wait on the protocol.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.11`: "b no shunt for now as I hope to get the actual bit for bit map of what the BLE would be from Ionic and or decode it myself as it is not encripted."

**What is already known and works.** The pack is an `IC-12V40-S9H` — Ionic 12 V 40 Ah S9H, four cells in series. Its BMS runs a Telink/HM-10-class transparent-serial module: service `FFE0`, characteristic `FFE1` used in both directions. Two independent reads, both proven from the car on 2026-09-08: the **advertisement's manufacturer data begins with pack millivolts**, broadcast with no connection at all; and a plain **Read or notification on `FFE1`** returns a framed packet — `7E` start, `01` type, `08` length, four little-endian uint16 cell counts, checksum, `0D` — which decodes at about **1.43 mV per count**, cross-checked because the four counts summed against the advertised pack voltage twice, four minutes apart. At the time of writing that is 3.25 V per cell and 13.0 V at the pack, on a one-count spread, which is a healthy balance.

**How the ESP32-C3 reads it.** Passive scan for the advertisement gives pack voltage with no connection, no pairing, nothing that can hang, and it keeps working while a phone is also connected. A GATT client subscribing to `FFE1` gives the cell frame, one connection at a time. Do both: scan always, connect only when cell detail is wanted. **`FEE7` and anything labelled DFU are never touched** — that is the firmware-update path on the BMS that runs the car's power, and the downside is a bricked pack.

**What this costs, stated plainly.** The type-01 frame is voltages. **Current and state of charge are not in it**, and reaching them means writing commands to `FFE1` against an undocumented protocol, either decoded here or supplied by Ionic. Until that lands the car logs pack and cell voltage and nothing else, and **D-280's sleeping-current target is not readable from the battery** — it stays the bench measurement at install 3.11, which it always was. A Victron SmartShunt remains the fallback that would give current, state of charge, consumed Ah and temperature, and would see every load outside the BMS's own terminals; it is deferred, not rejected, and the cargo bin is open once, so taking it up later is a bin job.

**In the data.** `parts` `P116` (the ESP32-C3 pair) keeps its place with the source now named. No shunt line is added. The CAN map keeps its battery-current and state-of-charge fields defined with no source behind them yet, marked so, rather than deleted — they are the shape the data will take when the protocol is known.

title: The master disconnect is the Blue Sea 9004e; its auxiliary pole is a switch-position input so the PMU drops excitation before the main contacts break
body:
**D-331 — The master disconnect is the Blue Sea 9004e; its auxiliary pole is a switch-position input so the PMU drops excitation before the main contacts break, and a high-joule TVS goes across the PMU main feed.** Camden's call, 2026-09-11, answering `00.12`: option (b).

**The hazard.** An unsuppressed load dump on a 12 V system is ISO 7637-2 pulse **5a — 65–87 V for 40–400 ms**, and reported lithium BMS disconnects run **120 V and above**. There are two triggers. Opening the master with the engine running is the avoidable one. **The BMS opening while driving** — over-current, cell fault, over-temperature — needs no mistake and never goes away: lead-acid degrades gracefully and stays in circuit, a BMS opens in milliseconds at full charge current.

**Why the aux pole is used this way and not the obvious way.** The 9004e carries an Alternator Field Disconnect pole whose contacts open slightly *before* the main contacts. On an externally regulated alternator it opens the field directly. D-316 fixed this car to the FB/FC alternator, which is **internally regulated**, so there is no external field to open. But the PMU already owns excitation on O12 → F15, so the aux pole is read instead as a **switch-position input**: the PMU sees the master about to open and drops excitation in logic before the main path breaks. Same protection, achieved through a channel the design already had.

**The TVS is independent of all of that.** A high-joule TVS across the PMU main feed at the module is the only thing that covers the BMS-opening case, which no switch can anticipate. It goes in whatever else is decided, and it is a couple of dollars. Separately, ECUMaster is to be asked directly whether the PMU's published "immunity according to ISO 7637" covers pulse **5a** unclamped or only **5b** — the TVS is fitted either way, so the answer changes nothing, it only tells us how much margin the module brings on its own.

**In the data.** `parts` `P049` becomes the 9004e; the SKU and price carry `confirm` until the cart is re-priced, which under D-323 has not happened. A high-joule TVS for the PMU main feed becomes its own `parts` row — it is not `P106`, which is the ICU carrier's own protection. The switch-position conductor runs the L4 leg from the cargo bin to the dash and takes a spare size-16 cavity in `L4-S2`, which had three free. **The PMU input it lands on is not assigned here** (`W-331`): `inputs` lists A1–A6, A8, A15 and A16 but not A7, which HO04 uses, so the table does not yet describe the module's real channel set. That is completed against the PMU's channel list first, and if no input is genuinely free it becomes a block rather than a guess.

title: The PMU-24 DL's channel set is complete - sixteen analog channels, six of them running as outputs, and not one position spare
body:
**D-333 — The PMU-24 DL's channel set is complete: it has sixteen analog channels, six of them are configured as outputs, and not one of the 39 positions is spare.** Agent, 2026-09-12, against `01-REFERENCE/PMU_info/PMU-24_Pinout_v1.0.pdf` and the manual's specification tables, completing `W-331` as D-331 required.

D-331 ended by saying the input for the master-switch position sense "is not assigned here" and that `inputs` "lists A1–A6, A8, A15 and A16 but not A7, so the table does not yet describe the module's real channel set." It does now, and the answer is worse than a missing row.

**What the module actually has.** Eight dedicated analog inputs **A1–A8**, 10-bit, 0–5 V, 20 V maximum, with software-selectable 10 kΩ pull-up or pull-down. Eight more channels **A9–A16** that **share their pins with outputs O17–O24** — 12-bit, 0–20 V, 30 V maximum, configurable as input *or* 7 A high-side output, one or the other. Then O1–O5 and O12–O16 at 25 A, and O6–O11 at 15 A, on their own pins.

**What this design does with them.** A1–A8 are all used: turn stalk, wiper stalk, brake and park, pop-up L, pop-up R, door jambs, **the oil-pressure node (A7)** and the hazard/horn/wink ladder. A9–A14 are all configured as **outputs** — O17 turn L, O18 turn R, O19 reverse, O20 interior, O21 start relay, O22 keep-alive. A15 and A16 are the headlight and key ladders, on the 12-bit side because they are read on the 12 V rail. O1–O16 are all assigned, with O13 and O14 capped for the swap. Counting: 22 outputs + 10 inputs + `+12V sw` + `+5V out` + ground + two CAN pairs = 39. **Every position.**

**So there is no free input and no free output.** `G12` asked me to write the expansion path down and assumed "all 22 outputs are allocated (two to the swap) and all ten inputs"; the truth is sixteen channels, not ten, and the six that look like spare inputs are already outputs. This is not a shortage that turns up at commissioning — it turns up the first time anyone wants one more thing, which is now.

**In the data.** `inputs` gains A7 and gains A9–A14 as `kind=output`, so the table finally describes the module's channel set rather than a subset of it; the enum widened to take `output`, deliberately, and `_tables` says what the table is now for. `rules spare-capacity` writes the growth path down: it starts at a relay socket, a fuse position, the O15 comfort bus, a capped module drop, or a second PMU — never at a channel. **`W-331` cannot be finished** and becomes `00.14`: which channel gives way, or does the sense go. The `L4-S2 6` conductor stays as drawn until that is answered.

title: Output health is a band around a measured baseline, and the low half of it is the module's own undercurrent flag
body:
**D-334 — An output's healthy current is a band around a measured baseline, never a typed number; the low half of the band is the module's own Min Current parameter, and channels below the module's measurement floor get no band at all.** Agent, 2026-09-12, carrying out `G1` against the PMU manual §9.1.

`G1` asked for "a `healthy_a` band per output in `pins.csv`, recorded at shakedown, and PMU logic rows that flag a lamp channel reading under half its baseline or a motor over 1.5× it." Two things changed in the doing.

**It is one stored number, not a band, because the band is derived (R2).** `pins.baseline_a` holds the current measured live at shakedown; the thresholds are `0.5 × baseline_a` low and `1.5 × baseline_a` high, and storing them would be two more numbers to drift. Nothing about `enable_a` changes — the soft fuse protects the wire and is sized from the conductor (D-279), and health is a different question asked of the same measurement.

**The low half already exists in the module.** The PMU's **Min Current** parameter raises status **2 UNDERCURRENT** and — this is the part that makes it usable — **does not switch the output off**. D-279 already said undercurrent is an annunciator and no logic may be built on it; the manual agrees in the same words. So bulb-out costs one configuration field per channel, not a function. The high half is a written function, because the module has no "running high but under the fuse" concept.

**The floor is the real constraint, and it rules two channels out.** Below a per-class threshold the PMU clips its own measurement to zero: about **0.5 A typical and up to 2 A** on the 25 A outputs, about **0.2 A** on the 15 A outputs, about **0.1 A** on the 7 A outputs. A channel whose baseline is not comfortably above its floor cannot have a band without crying wolf every time it is on. **O21 (start relay, 0.2 A) and O22 (keep-alive, 0.2 A)** are both 7 A channels sitting on their floor: they get none, and that is written down rather than discovered at shakedown. The 25 A channels are the ones to watch — HEAD_LOW at 3.0 A and HEAD_HIGH at 3.5 A are only a little above a floor that can be as high as 2 A, which is exactly why the number is measured and not computed from `est_a`.

**In the data.** `pins.baseline_a` added, blank on every row until CK01 fills it. `rules health-band` carries the derivation and the floors. `checks` CK01 is the shakedown box: exercise each circuit, read `pmu.oN.current` in the client, record the steady figure, and treat a gap of more than about 20 % against `est_a` as a tired part rather than a bad reading — which is D-025's replacement list, arriving as a by-product.

title: Retry is four named classes, and the pop-up bus is the one that must not retry
body:
**D-335 — Retry is four named classes, not one rule and not three, and the pop-up bus is the one that must not retry.** Agent, 2026-09-12, carrying out `G2` under D-279's policy.

D-279 split retry and latch by fault type but left every channel carrying the same "3 retries, 5 s". `G2` asked for three classes. Writing them out produced four, because one channel does not fit any of the three and pretending it does would be worse than an extra name.

- **lamp** — 3 retries at 5 s, then latch **and annunciate**. A latched stop lamp or headlamp that says nothing is worse than a flickering one (D-279). Eleven channels, including the accessory and comfort buses and the horn.
- **motor** — 5 retries at 15 s, no latch. A wiper stalled in snow or a blower against a blocked box is a thermal event that clears; the stall timer governs, not a current spike. Wipers high and low, blower, defog.
- **critical** — 1 retry at 2 s, then off until the key leaves RUN. A fuel pump or an ignition that trips twice in three seconds is a fault, and quietly retrying it forever is how a chafe becomes a fire. Fuel pump, ignition, start relay.
- **guarded** — 1 retry, then off and flag. **O1, the pop-up motor bus, and only O1.** An overcurrent here does not mean a marginal load; it means something is physically in the way, and a hand is the something. D-279 already noted O1 has no headroom — it sits at the 25 A ceiling against a measured 26 A both-sides stall — so its real handler is the D-186 obstruction timeout and retry exists only to ride out a cold morning.
- **none** — keep-alive and the two capped swap channels.

**Why a name and not just numbers.** The point of the column is that a channel cannot quietly differ from its peers: adding an output means choosing a class, and the class is the argument. The parameters map one-to-one onto the module's own Retry count / Retry every / Retry forever fields, so this is configuration, not firmware.

**In the data.** `logic.retry_class` added and set on all 21 rows; `logic.retry` rewritten from prose to the class's parameters; `rules retry-class` holds the definitions and the reasoning. No wire, no part.

title: The PMU cannot report an output stuck ON; it is inferred from output voltage against output state and it can only annunciate
body:
**D-336 — The PMU cannot report an output stuck ON. The condition is inferable from output voltage against output state, it is annunciation only, and the master disconnect stays the one hard kill.** Agent, 2026-09-12, reading the PMU manual §6.1 for `G3`.

`G3`'s premise is right and it is the failure mode this whole architecture inherits: **a relay fails open, a high-side MOSFET fails short.** An output stuck on runs its load with the key out and the module asleep.

**The manual is silent, and definitively so.** The complete output-status vocabulary is `0 OFF · 1 ACTIVE · 2 UNDERCURRENT · 3 OVERCURRENT · 7 THERMAL SHUTDOWN`. Every one of them is a story about how much current is flowing through an output the module believes it is driving. There is no state for "commanded off and still live", and no fault code, LED colour or CAN bit for it.

**It is detectable, and that is worth having.** The PMU measures **voltage** on every output — 0–16 V on the 25 A and 15 A pins, 0–20 V on the 7 A pins — and exposes it as `oN.voltage` alongside `oN.active`. Battery volts with `.active = 0` is a shorted switch, and a function saying so is three comparisons. `CK07` is that check at shakedown for O2, O3, O5, O7 and O12.

**But a detector is not a stop.** The thing doing the annunciating is the module that just failed, and the output it would need to drive to warn you is on the same silicon. So the honest statement is: this buys a diagnosis, not a protection. The protection is mechanical and it is the **master disconnect** — which is why `recovery` RC01 is "open the master disconnect before you touch anything", first, before any other step, and why it says a high-side FET fails short rather than assuming the reader knows.

**One thing the row did not know.** The PMU has a built-in **inertia switch** that drops every output when measured acceleration exceeds a configurable threshold, 6 G by default. That covers the crash case properly — as long as the module is alive, which is exactly the case a shorted FET is not.

**In the data.** `checks` CK07. `recovery` RC01 and the whole dead-module branch. `rules health-band` notes that undercurrent annunciates and does not stop. The row's last question — whether **O5, the fuel pump**, gets a series relay off the key's RUN ladder as a hardware back-stop — is Camden's, as the row said, and is **`00.15`**.

title: The PMU publishes no quiescent current, so D-280's measurement is the only number there will ever be
body:
**D-337 — ECUMaster publishes no quiescent or sleep current for the PMU, so D-280's bench measurement is the only number this design will ever have.** Agent, 2026-09-12, answering `G4`(a) against the manual.

`G4` asked me to "read the PMU's real sleep current from the manual and compute days-to-BMS-cutoff against the Ionic's capacity". The manual has no such figure. The specification tables give operating voltage (6–22 V), operating temperature, CPU, connectors and weight, and for outputs and inputs they are exhaustive — but there is no standby, sleep, quiescent or off-state current anywhere in 163 pages. D-280 already said as much and it is now confirmed rather than assumed.

**So the computation cannot be done and the arithmetic is already recorded.** D-280 carries it: on the 40 Ah pack, roughly **11 days at 150 mA and 80 days at 20 mA** before the BMS cuts off, with a bench measurement of an ECUMaster PMU reported at **under 20 mA**. The design's target is **≤ 30 mA, accept ≤ 50 mA**. Nothing here improves on that; what it does is close the door on getting the number from paper.

**Two things this run adds to it.** The pack's own cut-off is now recorded — **8.0 V** (00-CAR SP-232) — so the endpoint of that arithmetic is a real number rather than "flat". And `G4`'s (b), the clamp-meter box, is `CK02`: on the **battery negative cable**, engine off, one hour after key-off, which is a different reading from install 3.11's PMU-only bench figure and is the one that catches the amplifier, the head unit's constant through K11, the always-hot courtesy lamps on F19 and the pack's own BMS. Both are wanted; neither substitutes for the other.

**`G4`(c) is already ruled and was not re-asked.** The row proposed a Victron SmartShunt as `Q-128`. **D-330 declined it** on 2026-09-11 and took battery data from the Ionic's own BMS over BLE instead, deferring the shunt rather than rejecting it. A solved question governs every case like it.

**In the data.** `checks` CK02. `work` G4 done. No part, no wire, no change to LD17 — the estimate stands as an estimate until CK02 replaces it.

title: The PMU has a native delayed turn-off; the keep-alive expression may move into it, the wiring does not
body:
**D-338 — The PMU has a native delayed turn-off, so the keep-alive *expression* can move into it. The O22 conductor, its wake-strip diode and its drive to K11 do not move.** Agent, 2026-09-12, answering `V-075` from the manual §16.7.

`V-075` asked whether a configurable power-down delay makes the O22 self-hold latch unnecessary. **It exists.** The *Delayed turn off* panel (F9 in the client) gives **Turn off minimum time**, **Turn off maximum time** and a **Turn off channel**, and it requires exactly the wiring this design already has — a separate battery feed at the stud and a switched 12 V at pin 7. While the module is in that state `pmu.isTurningOff` reads 1, and turning the ignition back on restarts it half a second later.

**What may move.** D-248's rule set — release 30 s after the last input change with the key off and every door closed, and force release after 30 minutes whatever the doors read — is an expression today, held up by O22 feeding its own wake pin through a diode. That is a self-hold loop written in logic, and the panel does the same thing in the module's own firmware, with the force-off as a maximum time instead of a timer the logic has to run.

**What does not move, and this is the point of writing it down.** `V-075` said "the `KEEP_ALIVE` output (pin 8, O22) and its wake-strip diode are redundant and K11 can be driven from that delay instead." Only the first half survives contact with the pin list. **O22 also drives K11**, the head unit's constant master, and there is no spare output to hand that job to — D-333 has just established there is not one free position on the module. And the wake-strip diode costs nothing to leave in place while removing it is a wiring change at the dash node. So: the conductor stays, the diode stays, K11 stays on O22, and only the expression is a candidate to move. That is the reading that keeps the most options open, and it is free.

**One number the manual does not give.** It does not say what range *Turn off maximum time* accepts, and D-248 needs 30 minutes. If the field tops out below that, the expression stays exactly as written and nothing is lost. That is **`CK06`**, in the client at install §5.4 — a two-minute look, not a measurement on the car.

**In the data.** `checks` CK06; `work` V-075 done. `rules sleep` and `logic KEEP_ALIVE` are unchanged until CK06 says the panel can hold 30 minutes.

title: Two routing rules the benchmark earned: water enters from below or not at all, and the tach shield never runs beside a coil lead
body:
**D-339 — Two routing rules the production-car benchmark earned: everything enters a module from below or with a drip loop, and the shielded tach core never runs beside a coil lead.** Agent, 2026-09-12, carrying out `G7` and `G11`.

**Water (`G7`).** The classic Mercedes rear-SAM failure is water down a lamp seal or a blocked drain into a module. The FB's equivalents are the cowl seam and the windscreen, and the dash node sits in the footwell under both. `rules water-ingress`: every conductor enters the PMU, the dash node and each sill or rear panel **from below or with a drip loop**; nothing mounts in the **lowest 50 mm** of the footwell; the PMU's 39-way faces **down or sideways, never up**. Written now because moving a bracket while the dash is out costs nothing and moving it afterwards costs the dash. Where the water actually goes when the drains block is `CK04`, a look at M-1 — the rule does not wait on it.

**EMC (`G11`), with one correction to the premise.** The row said "the engine leg carries the CAN2 drop and the tach line past the coils and igniters." **The engine leg no longer carries CAN2 at all.** D-318 released `L1-S1 9` and `10` to sealing plugs and moved every computer, including a future ECU, to the dash node. So the engine-bay exposure is the **shielded tach core** alone — and it is the worst run in the car, because it takes a trailing-coil negative primary past four coil and igniter leads. `rules emc-routing`: it crosses ignition leads at **90°** and never runs parallel to one within **50 mm**, with the drain to the GND bus at the dash-node end only, which the record already specified. CAN2's only remaining exposure is inside the dash, where the same 50 mm applies past the blower and wiper motor leads and the O1 pop-up motor bus.

**In the data.** `rules water-ingress`, `rules emc-routing`, `checks` CK04. Both are install rules, so they govern how L1 and the dash node are **laid**, not only how they are drawn. No wire, no part, no cavity.

title: Two conventions written down: a cavity number is the moulding, and the fuse-lid card is a query
body:
**D-340 — Two conventions written down: a cavity number is the number moulded into the housing, and the fuse-lid card is a query rather than a document.** Agent, 2026-09-12, carrying out `G14` and `G10`.

**Cavity numbers (`G14`).** Every OEM harness print states its view convention at the top — wire side or mating side — because a mirror-image reading is the classic way to build a perfect harness backwards. This record has no such convention and does not need one, and that is the thing to say out loud: **a cavity number here is the number moulded into the housing itself.** Read it off the part. That is a reason the DT family suits this build — the number is on the moulding, so there is nothing to mirror. A factory plug is different: `lands_on` carries Mazda's terminal **letter** from the factory diagram, not a cavity number, and the two never share a cell. The row asked for one sentence at the head of a wire-tables document; in v3 the home for a convention is `rules`, where the check can see it.

**The fuse-lid card (`G10`).** Every OEM junction block carries its map on the lid; here the map is a config sheet in a binder, which is the same problem one layer up. The row asked for "a template and a view". **CLAUDE.md §1 forbids the view**, and rightly: `DECISIONS.md` is the one generated document and the visual layer is a later concern. But the card's content is entirely derived, so it does not need a template — it needs a query, and `rules fuse-lid-card` carries the two `sql` lines that print it: the outputs with their circuits and soft-fuse limits, and the fuse positions with their labels and feeds. Printed and laminated when there is something to print with, one at the dash node and one in the glovebox beside the laptop port. Because it is a query it can never disagree with the record, which is the only reason a card is allowed to exist at all.

**In the data.** `rules cavity-numbers`, `rules fuse-lid-card`. Nothing generated, nothing to keep in step.

title: The bundle-derating audit changes nothing, because no conductor in this harness is loaded above 10 A continuous
body:
**D-341 — The bundle-derating audit finds nothing to change: every 16 AWG conductor on a channel enabled above 10 A is a tap already marked as one, and no conductor in this harness, at any gauge, is loaded continuously above 10 A.** Agent, 2026-09-12, carrying out `G8`.

`G8`'s concern is a good one. OEMs run sealed 1.5 mm contacts at about **10 A continuous in a loom**, not at their 13 A single-contact rating, because a bundle cannot shed heat the way a bench test can — and D-232 lets 16 AWG sit at exactly 13.0 A. The question was which conductors that actually bites.

**The query.** Five 16 AWG conductors sit on a channel enabled above 10 A: `DP-ICU-A 1`, `DP-DCU 1`, `DP-KEY 3` and `L4-S 4` off **O10** at 13.0 A, and `DP-ICU-B 12` off **O3** at 13.0 A. **All five already carry `src_note=tap`**, which is precisely the exception D-232 wrote — four of them are the cases D-232 named and the fifth is the road-speed sensor supply D-272 added later, correctly marked when it was added.

**And none of them carries current.** The ICU's logic rail draws about 0.8 A peak; the two capped module drops draw nothing; the road-speed sensor draws milliamps; the high-beam tell-tale sense is an input to a divider. The 13.0 A is the **channel's soft fuse**, sized to protect the 14 AWG branch behind it, not a description of the conductor's load. That distinction is the whole answer.

**Checked the other way too.** No 14 AWG conductor is loaded above 10 A either: O8 and O9 are held at 13.0 A by the DT contact rating (D-223) but draw 4.0 A and 5.5 A; O11 is enabled at 13.0 A and draws 6.0 A. The largest continuous load in the harness on anything smaller than 12 AWG is the horn at 6.0 A. There is nothing for OEM bundle derating to bite on.

**In the data.** Nothing. That is the finding, and it is worth a decision precisely so nobody runs the query again in six months.

title: Route lengths become a measured table; the wire schedule and W-329 wait on M-2 rather than on another estimate
body:
**D-342 — Route lengths become a measured table. The wire schedule, and `W-329` with it, wait on M-2 rather than on another estimate.** Agent, 2026-09-12, carrying out `G13` and re-gating `W-329`.

`W-329` asked me to recompute the 16 AWG RED family after D-329 removed `L2-S 6`, and D-329 was explicit that this is "a derived figure … recomputed from the wire schedule, never by hand here." **It cannot be recomputed, because the record contains no lengths.** Not one: `cavities` has gauge and colour and destination but no distance, `cables` has feet for the eleven heavy runs and nothing else does. The ~510 ft that D-256 quoted against a 500 ft spool was never derived from the cavity table — it was D-202's hand estimate at 1.5×, and subtracting one front-leg conductor from it by eye would be exactly the hand arithmetic D-329 refused.

**Rivian's lesson is the right one and it is not about the estimate.** They took 1.6 miles of wire out by *measuring* what a zonal layout needed. Here the footage is the design, and it is the one derived fact still typed.

**So the table exists now and the numbers wait.** `routes` — leg, from, to, via, feet — with **21 rows and every `ft` blank**: the five L1 runs, four L2, five L3, five L4 and the sill, each naming the grommet or path the tape follows. M-2 is now a checklist rather than a memory test, which matters because the interior comes apart once (D-202) and a route not measured that day is a route estimated forever. The cut length stays 1.5× the measured route.

**Consequence for the carts.** `W-329` is gated on `G13` and `G13` on `C1`'s M-2. If the 16 AWG RED family does come in under the 500 ft spool, `P009` — the 50 ft WireBarn cut D-256 added — leaves the order. Nothing is paid before then anyway (D-323), so the sequence costs nothing.

**In the data.** New table `routes`, 21 rows, `ft` blank. `work` G13 gated on C1, W-329 gated on G13, both with the reason in the note rather than in someone's memory.

title: The kick-down gets its own inline fuse off the ignition output and three conductors, and rides the tunnel run that is already there
body:
**D-343 — The kick-down gets its own 5 A inline fuse off the ignition output and three conductors, and it rides the tunnel run the road-speed pair is already using.** Agent, 2026-09-12, carrying out `W-320` under D-320.
