title: The ICU carrier's Teensy 4.1 pin map: CAN1 on 22/23, the tach and road speed on FreqMeasureMulti pins 2 and 3, the BT817 on single-lane SPI0 (10-13, PDN 9), and every channel promoted into icu_channels.teensy_pin
body:
**D-377 — The ICU carrier's Teensy 4.1 pin map.** CAN1 is on 22 / 23. The tach and road speed are on FreqMeasureMulti pins 2 and 3. The BT817 runs on single-lane SPI0 (10–13, PDN 9), not QSPI. Every channel's pin is now in `icu_channels.teensy_pin`. This is the agent's call (§3 small): it moves copper on a board that has not been laid out and changes no harness wire, part or price. It is step A2 of the layout guide, done before any measurement because nothing about it is measured.

**Sources.** CAN pins come from the ACAN_T4 manual (tables 2 and 5: FlexCAN1 Rx 23 / Tx 22, FlexCAN2 1 / 0, FlexCAN3 30 / 31). Analog, SPI0 and Wire pins come from the Teensy core's `pins_arduino.h` (A0–A13 = 14–27, A14–A17 = 38–41, SPI 10 / 11 / 12 / 13, SDA 18 / SCL 19). Serial2 comes from `HardwareSerial2.cpp` (RX 7 / TX 8). Capture-capable pins come from FreqMeasureMulti's IMXRT table (0–9, 22–25, 28, 29, 33, 36, 37, 42–54 on the 4.1) and FreqMeasure's page (Teensy 4.x: pin 22 only). All were read 2026-09-22. PJRC's printed pinout card was not readable as text: check it against this map when the socket footprint is placed, per A2's own instruction.

**What it settled.**
- **Tach capture vs CAN.** The record said "input capture" for IC04 / IC08 and "CAN1" for IC16. The obvious library, FreqMeasure, has exactly one Teensy 4.x pin, 22, which is CAN1's TX. So the tach and road speed use FreqMeasureMulti, on 2 and 3. The firmware has no tach capture yet, so nothing changes in code; the bench rig `tach_simulator` keeps its own 3 → 4 jumper.
- **The display bus (guide A0 #5).** `icu_channels` IC21 said "SPI1 / QSPI"; `bt817.h` drives SPI0 (CS 10, PDN 9) at 20 MHz single-lane and says QSPI is a later optimisation. The Teensy 4.1's only QSPI port is FlexSPI2 on the bottom pads, and the PSRAM (P108) is soldered there. So single-lane SPI0 it is: the firmware was right and the row changes. IO2 / IO3 are still wired, to 26 / 27, and held as inputs so a later software QSPI is not foreclosed.
- **Consequence, arithmetic.** A full-screen push is 614,400 B × 8 bit / 30 MHz ≈ 165 ms (≈ 250 ms at the 20 MHz bring-up clock). The archived "~100 ms" assumed QSPI. It is still only a page transition (D-168: dirty tiles in the loop), so nothing else moves. `params.full_push_ms` now derives it.
- **Lines the sheet has and the record didn't.** The schematic's J5 carries CAN_STB, BT817_INT, BL_EN and PG_5V, which the rows never listed. They are placed on IC16 (STB 32), IC21 (INT 24), IC13 (BL_EN 36) and IC12 (PG_5V 37).

**The map.** ADC: IC01 14 · IC02 15 · IC03 16 · IC05 17 · IC07 20 · IC14 21. Capture: IC04 2 · IC08 3. Digital: IC06 28 · IC09 29 · IC10 30 · IC11 31 · IC22 25. CAN1: 22 / 23, STB 32. BT817: 10–13, PD 9, INT 24, IO2 26, IO3 27. I²C: 18 / 19, IMU INT 33. Radio: Serial2 7 / 8, EN 34, BOOT 35. BL_EN 36, PG_5V 37. **Spare:** 0 / 1 (CAN2 / Serial1), 4 / 5 / 6 (capture), 38–41 (analog). Nothing on 42–54 (the SD slot and the PSRAM pads).

**In the data.** `icu_channels` `teensy_pin` on all 19 rows that reach the Teensy; IC21 `carrier_stage`, `on_the_wire` and `note` (SPI, and its stale "the pages are the luxury package's", D-374). `params` `full_push_ms`. The sheet's `J5` still carries ordinal numbers, and its nets are still named `QSPI_*`. Renumbering them against the socket footprint is guide step A2.4, in KiCad.

title: The PMU's frames 0x100-0x130 are a CANbus Export we define, not a layout ECUMaster fixes; fail-open is a per-input default and on-timeout value
body:
**D-378 — The PMU's frames 0x100–0x130 are a CANbus Export we define, not a layout ECUMaster fixes. Fail-open (D-251) is built from each CAN input's own default and on-timeout value.** The agent's reading of the PMU manual in the tree (S-028, `01-REFERENCE/PMU_info/PMU_Manual.pdf`, ECUMaster PMU-16/16DL/16AS/24DL User Manual v101.2.1, 2026-04-23), closing work row V-065.

**What the record believed.** V-065 and `can_messages` 0x100 said the PMU's CAN layout is "fixed by ECUMaster", so every PMU-sourced field in the ICU was "written against a guess".

**What the manual says.** The PMU has two separate transmit mechanisms:
- **The Standard CAN Stream is fixed** (p.95: "Parameters themselves are predefined (they are fixed and cannot be configured)"). It uses Base ID +0…+11, 0x668 by default on PMU-24 #1, at 20 or 62.5 Hz: status, currents, voltages and temperatures. It is not what 0x100–0x130 describe.
- **The CANbus Export is ours** (p.90: "CANbus Export allows sending any available channel of the device. Frames with any CAN ID can be transmitted on one of two CAN buses"). It allows DLC 0–8, 1–100 Hz or on an edge, and at most 500 frames/s per bus (p.91). Our four frames are 40 frames/s. CAN2 defaults to 500 kbps. The only reserved IDs are 0x012–0x017 on CAN1 (p.94).

**The limits that bind our layouts.** An Export field is 8-bit (unsigned or signed) or 16-bit (big- or little-endian), times an integer multiplier 1–1000, or raw (p.92). The manual shows no bit-packing, no multiplexing and no rolling counter on transmit. So:
- the bitfield bytes (0x100 bytes 1 and 2, 0x120 bytes 2–4) need PMU math channels that build the packed value;
- **0x130's multiplexed channel index and the byte-7 counters on 0x100–0x130 are unproven.** They are proved in the PMU client at F-009, or 0x130 becomes fixed frames instead.

**Fail-open.** Each CAN input has a default "used from starting the device until receiving the first frame" (p.89). The timeout is set per message object, in seconds. What happens on timeout is set per input: "Use previous value" or "Set value". D-251's fail-open is therefore: a safe default on every input near a control rule, with "Set value" to that same safe value on timeout. The 0x218 fault log comes from the same timeout. Whether the message-object timeout accepts fractions of a second (our 250 / 500 ms) is new check **CK13**.

**In the data.** `work` V-065 done; F-009 re-scoped (prove the Export in the client, or simplify the frames). `can_messages` 0x100–0x130 notes. `checks` CK13 (new).

title: The DCU carrier's parts check (V-083): protected low-side switches for the seats, 65 V-rated high-side switches, one quad half-bridge for the mirrors, and a 5 A buck for the servo rail
body:
**D-379 — The DCU carrier's parts check (V-083).** The seat loads use protected low-side switches (Infineon BTS3011TE) instead of bare FETs. The window commands and mirror heat use 65 V-rated PROFET+ high-side switches (BTT6200-4ESA, BTT6050-1ERA). The mirrors run from one quad half-bridge (TI DRV8962-Q1). The servo rail gets its own 5 A buck (TI TPS54560B-Q1) and the firmware moves one servo at a time. The agent's call, closing work row V-083 as D-273 did for the ICU: every part was checked against its datasheet, and every price and suffix stays `confirm` until it is ordered.

**What the check changed, and why.**
- **The AOD4184 cannot be driven from the Teensy.** Its gate threshold is up to 2.6 V, and its on-resistance is only specified at 4.5 V and above. At 3.3 V a worst-case part is barely on, and it is not AEC-Q101. The **BTS3011TE** (TO252-5) takes a 3.0–5.5 V logic supply, is 11 mΩ (22 mΩ hot), is rated 10 A nominal, and has its own short-circuit and over-temperature protection. That protection matters on a seat heater, which is a safety load (§3). Its load-dump rating is 40 V with a 2.2 Ω load: `confirm` it against the comfort supply's clamp.
- **The high-side switches are the 24 V PROFET+ family, because of the clamp.** The SMBJ33A clamps load dump at ~53 V, and the 12 V PROFET+2 (BTS70xx) is only rated to 35 V, so it was rejected. **BTT6200-4ESA** (quad, 1 A per channel with all four on, 3.3 V inputs, VS(LD) 65 V) takes the four window commands (SN22). **BTT6050-1ERA** (4.5 A nominal, 65 V) takes mirror heat (SN16), which V-101 puts at ~3 A for the pair.
- **The mirrors use one chip.** The **DRV8962-Q1** has four independent 5 A half-bridges, 4.5–60 V, and 1.5 V logic threshold. Three drive the motor common and the left and right motors; the fourth holds its low FET on as the clutch-coil sink (D-360). The TLE94104EP was rejected as a 40 V-class part under the clamp. The mirror stall current is still W-332's; it is assumed under 1.5 A, far inside 5 A.
- **K3/K4 selects:** Nexperia **PMV37ENEA** (SOT-23, 60 V, AEC-Q101, Vgs(th) 2.3 V max). That leaves ~1 V of overdrive at 3.3 V into a ~150 mA relay coil. The on-resistance at 2.5 V is a curve, not a guarantee: `confirm` on the bench.
- **The servo rail outgrew the LMR36015.** Three servos stalled together is up to 7.5 A. A 5 A **TPS54560B-Q1** (HSOP-8, 60 V, load-dump tolerant, with a 60 V 5 A Schottky catch diode, `confirm` part), plus firmware that moves one servo at a time, keeps the realistic peak near 2.5–3 A. That rule goes to F-017. The logic rail stays an **LMR36015-Q1**, as on the ICU.
- **Current sense:** **INA180A1** (gain 20, powered from 3V3) across **two 10 mΩ 2512 ≥ 2 W resistors in parallel** (5 mΩ). These are easy to buy and share the heat. 18 A worst case (V-101) is 1.8 V at the ADC, with full scale about 33 A.
- **CAN:** **TCAN1042HVDRQ1**. The V suffix gives the VIO pin (3.3 V logic); the H suffix gives ±70 V bus-fault protection.

**In the data.** `parts` P146 (the two bucks, now different parts), P149 (the comfort stage's parts), P145 (the exact suffix). `dcu_channels` SN13, SN16, SN17, SN22, SN23, SN27 carrier_stage. `work` V-083 done; F-017 note (servo sequencing).

title: The control panel's electronics: nine keys on a diode-isolated 3 × 3 matrix, four detented encoders, the thumbstick, all on one 20-way IDC ribbon to the DCU
body:
**D-380 — The control panel's electronics.** Nine keys on a 3 × 3 matrix with a diode on every key, four detented quadrature encoders, and the mirror thumbstick. All of it reaches the DCU on one 20-way 2.54 mm IDC ribbon, whose pinout is the new table `panel_ribbon`. The agent's call, closing work row H-007's electrical half: every part of it can be undone by editing rows, and nothing is bought, cut or wired yet. The panel's look is not part of it: where the keys and knobs sit and what they look like is the luxury package's (luxury LP20, FT14), a block when the faceplate is drawn.

**The design.**
- **Keys** (FT14's nine): ROW1 defog · hatch release · fuel-door release. ROW2 HVAC mode · recirculate · window DRV up. ROW3 window DRV down · PASS up · PASS down. One 1N4148W per key, so any combination reads true: two windows moving at once is the normal case, and a diode-less matrix ghosts on three keys. Rows are driven low one at a time; columns are pulled up and carry pin-change interrupts. **Asleep, all three rows are held low, so any key press interrupts and wakes the DCU**, which then pulls the PMU's wake strip on DP-DCU 6 (D-355, SN21). That is how the panel works with the key out.
- **Encoders:** fan, temperature, and one knob per seat. A seat knob turns clockwise from OFF for heat 1–3 and anticlockwise for cool 1–3, so heat and cool can never both be on (D-073). The interlock lives in the knob as well as the firmware. Detents and range are firmware (D-355), and there is nothing to calibrate on the panel.
- **Thumbstick** (D-359): two pots fed from the Teensy's 3.3 V on their own analog ground (ribbon pin 20), plus a push to GND.
- **The ribbon:** 20 conductors, as DV53 foresaw ("sixteen to twenty"). It carries no 12 V: the panel's illumination stays a separate lead from L3-S1 8.

**In the data.** `panel_ribbon` (new table, 20 rows); `dcu_channels` SN18, SN19, SN20; `parts` P155, P157; `devices` DV53; `work` H-007 done. F-017 does the scan, the encoders and sending 0x400 (F-016).

title: The door and A8 wake stages' values: excitation 220k switched off while awake, sense divider 1M / 560k, a 1 µF edge into a follower, pulse about 0.4 s - all confirm until CK12
body:
**D-381 — The door and A8 wake stages' values.** The agent's call, closing work row A10 on the topology A10 found and the pulse D-375 ruled. The values are the new table `wake_stages`. Nothing is bought: every part comes from P072 (2N3904), P069 (the E24 kit), P071 (1N5819 spares) and P158 (the film capacitors). Every value is `confirm` until CK12 measures the three facts no document gives.

**Per side, three 2N3904s, plus one shared:**
- **Excitation, only while asleep.** Q1, a follower off the F3 switch supply, feeds the ladder line through **220k**. Awake, the shared Q0 (driven from O22) holds both Q1 bases at 0 V, so the line sees only the PMU's own 10 kΩ pull-up and the readings don't shift. Q1's E-B junction then sits 4.1 V reverse-biased, under its 6 V limit.
- **Sense.** Q2 reads the line through a **1M / 560k** divider. At rest (the 47k baseline, D-368) the line sits at 1.99–2.41 V over 12.0–14.4 V, putting Q2's base at 0.71–0.86 V: on. With the highest-resistance pressed state (19.4k) the line is 0.92–1.11 V and the base 0.33–0.40 V: off, even hot. Awake, the line is at 4.1 V, Q2 is hard on, and **no pulse is ever made while the PMU is already awake**. The thin margin is cold at 12.0 V at rest, which CK12 reads.
- **The pulse (D-375).** Q2's collector (100k pull-up) rises on a press. A **1 µF** film capacitor carries that edge to Q3, a follower held off by **470k**, which drives the wake-strip input into the strip's 10 kΩ drain at about 10 V. That fixes the failure A10 found in the v2 stage, which reached only ~1.1 V. The pulse lasts roughly C × 420 kΩ ≈ 0.4 s; 2.2 µF would give ≈ 0.9 s. A **1N5819 clamp** on Q3's base takes the negative edge when the switch is released, which would otherwise exceed the 6 V limit. A held switch makes one pulse and nothing more, so a door left ajar cannot keep the car awake (D-248).

**What CK12 settles:** (i) the pins' resistance to ground with the PMU unpowered; (ii) pin 7's switching threshold and current; (iii) the PMU's boot time, which sizes the capacitor. Plus the cold rest margin. If a reading moves a value, the row changes before anything is soldered (E7 and E15 wait on A10).

**In the data.** `wake_stages` (new table, 27 rows). `parts` P069 and P071 used_for. `checks` CK12 note. `work` A10 done.

title: The DCU's comfort circuits: 7.5 A per seat heater, 5 A per seat cooler, 5 A for mirror heat, and an 8-way DT13 comfort connector with its own two ground pins
Each harness leg gets two generated drawings - a pin ladder (A) and a route map (B) - under 00-electrical/diagrams, rebuilt by rx7.py diagrams; the four options are kept for a later switch
body:
**D-385 — Every harness leg gets two generated drawings: a pin ladder (A) and a route map (B), in `00-electrical/diagrams/<leg>/`, rebuilt by `rx7.py diagrams`. The four sampled options are kept for a later switch.** Camden's call, 2026-09-23, in conversation after he was shown four options sampled on real L1 data.

**His words.** First: "i want a map of each leg of the harness on an easy to read diagram for my use while building and for the car record for later … we need a way to have the diagrams dialed in color coded and perfect no overlaping text or wires other the a one over one cross." Then, choosing: "all options this round are good store them for futre refrence in case i want to switch, for now follow the A and B plan for each leg, in 00-electrical make a dir diarams with a readme with these options, and a folder for each led with two files for each leg (a and b)."

**The ruling.**
- **A · Pin ladder.** One block per housing and one row per cavity, with each wire a straight line from its cavity to `cavities.lands_on`. Crossings are impossible by construction.
- **B · Route map.** The leg as it runs in the car, drawn like a transit map: each wire is its own line, stacked in branch order, so it peels off the outside of the bundle. Bends are 45° only and nothing crosses.
- **Files.** Each leg's two sheets are `A-pin-ladder.svg` and `B-route-map.svg` in `L1-engine/`, `L2-front/`, `L3-dash/` and `L4-rear/`.
- **Options kept.** The C (ELK) and D (D2) samples, and the A and B samples, are kept in `diagrams/options/` with the code that drew them. `diagrams/README.md` records each option's verdict.

**Why it is safe to generate.** This amends CLAUDE.md §1, which allowed only `DECISIONS.md` and `TODO.md`, under the same four conditions:
- the sheets are a pure projection of the record
- they are read-only
- they are rebuilt whole by one command
- nothing gates a commit on them, and `check` never looks at them

**The overlap rule, which is what makes it work.** Every label is measured with the real font before it is placed. A sheet with two touching labels, or a label on a wire, is refused and not written, and the command exits 2. The WireViz sheets (D-275 / D-276) failed because nothing checked the layout.

**Consequences in the data.** Two columns were added, both small (§3: a fact that had no column):
- **`devices.route`** (ref `routes.id`) is set only where a route's `to_node` or note names the device: DV01–DV07, DV10–DV16, DV18–DV20, DV22, DV23, DV25, DV27–DV29, DV31, DV34, DV36–DV38, DV40, DV41, DV43, DV47, DV48, DV50 and DV51. DV41 (jamb switches) is on RT19 because its conductor ends at the sill splice.
- **`cavities.route`** is used only for a conductor with no device at its far end:
  - L2-S 4 on RT09 ("run to the wiper branch")
  - L2-S 5 on RT06 (the nose)
  - L3-P 2, L3-S2 3–6 and L3-S3 5–8 on RT11, which RT11's note names
  - L4-P 3–4, L4-M 9–12 and L4-S2 1–5 on RT19 (the sill node)
  - L4-S 5–7 on RT15 (the rear-node receptacle)

**Left blank on purpose (R11).** The record does not say which run these take:
- devices: the brake fluid switch DV08, hazard DV21, wink switches DV24, parking brake DV26, dash illumination DV30, defog DV33, interior lamp DV39 and fuel-door solenoid DV49
- cavities: L2-M 8, and the L3-MOD and L3-RDR receptacles

They are drawn under "No route in the record yet". Setting the column moves them onto their branch.

title: The electrical project splits into 00-design and 01-build, each with its own generated TODO; nothing in build starts before the design is reviewed and frozen (phase SOURCING); the 2026-09-23 risk review becomes work and blocks

**The risk review, factored in.**

title: The car comes apart once: the design list ends with the interior stripped (all wiring left in place) and the measurements that need it out; the build list starts from the interior out and ends with it back in
body:
**D-387 — The car comes apart once. The design list ends with the interior stripped (every wire left in place) and the measurements that need it out; the build list starts from the interior out and ends with it back in.** Camden's call, 2026-09-23. It refines D-386.

**His words.** "this is good but we need better sepatation of car apart and not, design todo should end with all things that need dash and inteerior out, then build starts there interiror out to put back in. but make it maore segragated and incude the block step of strip the car inteerior (leave all wirirng)"

**Reading taken.** "The block step" is read as a single step, the strip, not a question in BLOCKS.md.

**The ruling.**
- **Design Part 1: car whole.** Desk, bench and anything done on the car as it stands.
- **S1: strip the interior** (new, his). Out come the seats, console, centre stack, dash and cluster (unplugged, not cut), glovebox, carpet, kick and sill panels, and the cargo-bin trim. Nothing electrical is cut, unpinned or moved. Fasteners are bagged and labelled, and every connector and loom run is photographed where it lies (M-7). S1 waits on every Part 1 row, so the car is off the road as short a time as possible.
- **Design Part 2: interior out.** S1 first, then everything that needs the car apart:
  - C1 (the measurement day, M-1 to M-7), C3, C4 and V-102 now gate on S1.
  - A5, Q-014, Q-110, Q-115, V-055, V-081, V-088, G13 and W-329 follow through C1.
  - H-002 gates on S1 directly, because it waits on the mirror heads measured at the door plug (luxury W-332).
  - Then the design review (Z1) and his freeze (Z2).
- **Build Part 3: car apart.** Parts arrive, then the backbone, the dash node, the legs, the migration, the full function check and the factory harness out.
- **Build Part 4: interior back in.** E35 is new: the cabin looms are final-wrapped and photographed before the dash closes, then the reverse of S1. After it come the shakedown drives, E31 to E34, and E31 now gates on E35.
- **How it is recorded.** `_project` names the two boundary rows (`car_apart` = S1, `car_back` = E35). `rx7.py todo` derives each row's part from its gate, so no row carries a typed section.

- **E33's final wrap** is now the engine bay only. The cabin looms are wrapped at E35, before the dash goes back.

- **Block `00.29`** (how the car runs during migration) is sharpened. The car cannot be driven during the migration under either option now.

**Consequence to know.** The car is off the road from S1 until E35. That span includes the design review, the freeze, the sourcing and shipping of every part, and the whole build.

title: Planning is open in every project at every phase: the phase says how far the build has got, never whether design may be touched
body:
# D-398 - Planning is open in every project at every phase: the phase says how far the build has got, never whether design may be touched

*2026-09-24 - Camden*

**Decision.** **Planning is open in every project at every phase. Design work, blocks and parts rounds may be taken up in any project at any time, whether it is PROPOSED, PLANNING, SOURCING or BUILDING. A project's phase records how far its build has got. It never closes planning, and one project's phase never holds another's.** Camden's call, 2026-09-24, in chat: *"please update the rx7 block structure that allows planning to be open for any project any time"*.

**Why.** Nothing in `tools/rx7.py` limited planning by phase. `block`, `new`, `add` and the gate resolver never read it, and `02-engine` already had READY design rows while PROPOSED. The limit was in the words of `CLAUDE.md`: §6.1 was headed "phase PROPOSED or PLANNING", §6.5 "any phase ≥ PLANNING", and the freeze read as the end of design. That would have stopped a project from being planned at all once its build started, and stopped a new idea (a seat, a lamp, a sensor) from being worked on in a project already buying parts.

**What the freeze still does.** It stays Camden's ruling and still moves a project to SOURCING. Every build row still gates on `phase:SOURCING` (D-386), so nothing is bought or cut before the first verified design. What changes is that the freeze starts the build without ending planning.

**Design opened after the freeze.** The phase never moves back. The new row goes on the design track, and every build row it changes gets the new row's id in its gate, so only the affected work waits and the rest of the build carries on. Undoing work already done (re-cutting, re-ordering, re-wiring) is still §3's irreversible, so it is a block.

**In the data.** No rows change. The phase values, the gates and the tool stay as they are. `CLAUDE.md`: the §1 build-track paragraph, §6.1 (heading, the new opening paragraph, and step 7), and §6.5's heading.

title: The agent commits and pushes: small commits that each say what changed and why, straight to master, never a pull request
body:
# D-401 - The agent commits and pushes: small commits that each say what changed and why, straight to master, never a pull request

*2026-09-24 - Camden*

**Decision.** **The agent commits and pushes at the end of every run, straight to `master`, and Camden no longer does. Commits are small, one change each, and each message says what changed and why with its decision ids. There are no pull requests and no branches unless he asks.** Camden's call, 2026-09-24, in chat: *"please adjust the rules of this project, you have full commit and push power, please help me keep the reposity up to date and full of usefull commits but no PR's. then please commit and push all these changes to main"*.

**Why.** §2 left `git commit` to him, so work sat uncommitted between sessions, and the history shows it: "poopy long commit", "begin todo", "pbc part 1", a whole round of decisions in one commit (D-385 - D-396). Committing is not a call only he can make. It records what the run already did, and `check` guards it through the pre-commit hook.

**"main" is `master`.** He said "push to main". The repository's only branch, and GitHub's default, is `master`. Pushing to a new `main` would have split the history into two branches, so "main" is read as the main branch, `master` (§3: the reading that keeps the most options open). Renaming the branch is his call if he wants it.

**The rules** (`CLAUDE.md` §6.10): one change per commit, each leaving `check` clean; a subject that names the change and its decision ids, and a body that gives the why; push after committing; never force-push, rewrite pushed history or skip the hook; a failed push is reported, not retried with force; his writing pages are committed as they stand.

**In the data.** No rows change. `CLAUDE.md`: §2 (Camden no longer commits; the agent keeps the repository current), the run ending in §6, the new §6.10, and a `PUSHED` line in the §8 report.

title: The ladder margin budget (R3): A4 and A5 decode on upward windows because a ground offset only raises a reading; A15 and A16 decode on the switch's conductance against the measured supply; CK14-CK16 measure what the budget assumes
body:
**D-408 — The ladder margin budget (R3): the fixed ±windows fail inside the design's own acceptance limits. A4 and A5 decode on upward windows, because a ground offset can only raise a reading. A15 and A16 decode on the switch's conductance, computed against the PMU's measured supply voltage, so supply sag and charge voltage drop out. Three new checks measure what the budget assumes: CK14 (a real crank at MG23), CK15 (can the PMU client do the division), CK16 (a pop-up cycle at MG15 / MG16). Software only: no wire, no part, no money.** Agent, 2026-09-24, R3 (D-386 risk review). Nobody was asked; §3 small, because every change here is PMU configuration and rows, and R3 itself names the fix ("widen windows or move references, and add a check").

**The model.** A1-A8: the internal 10 kΩ pull-up to 5 V (D-018), 10-bit, about 204.6 counts per volt. A15 / A16: the 100 kΩ bias from +5 V (D-167) against the channel's own resistance to ground, which D-184's published centres fix at 10 kΩ (OFF 93, PARK 604 at a 12.0 V feed) and 4096 counts over 20 V. The 10 kΩ is inferred from those numbers, not from a datasheet: *confirm* at E26 from the OFF reading (R11). Windows are ± half-widths around the live reading (D-142).

**A16 — supply sag and charge voltage.** A summed ladder fed from battery voltage reads in proportion to it. Calibrated at E26 with every output off, the battery at rest near 13.3 V: RUN reads 1326, START 1906, window ±200. With the alternator at 14.6 V, RUN reads 1450 - inside, with 76 counts left. But START leaves its window as soon as the voltage at the key falls under **11.9 V while cranking**, and at 10.5 V it reads 1511 - which is RUN's window. `rules crank` releases O21 when A16 leaves START, so a crank that sags the pack releases the start relay, the sag recovers, START returns: the starter chatters. A LiFePO4 pack under a rotary starter sagging into the 11s is not unusual, and nobody has measured this one (CK14).

**A15 — the same arithmetic, found on the way.** Window ±75. HEAD_LO read at 13.3 V is 1326; at 14.6 V charging it is 1450, 124 counts up, out of its window - the headlamps' decode leaves its window whenever the alternator is charging. HEAD_HI and PASS overlap outright across 11.5-14.8 V. It is fixed with A16 because it is the same fix.

**The fix for A15 and A16: decode the conductance, not the voltage.** Each ladder is a conductance G switched between the feed V and the node; the node is v = (V·G + 5/Rb) / (G + 1/Rb + 1/Rin). Solved for G with V = the PMU's own measured supply: **g = (k1·v − k2) / (V − v)**, with k1 = 1/Rb + 1/Rin = 0.110 and k2 = 5/Rb = 0.050 (per kΩ, volts), refitted at E26 so that OFF reads g = 0 (k2 = k1 × the OFF reading in volts). g is independent of V. States: OFF 0 · ACC / PARK 0.030 · RUN / HEAD_LO 0.097 · START 0.244 (0.214 if ACC drops in START, D-055) · HEAD_HI 0.219 · PASS 0.522. Boundaries: **0.015 · 0.055 · 0.150**, and on A15 also **0.340**. A 0.3 V difference between the PMU's supply sense and the key's feed moves START's g by under 9 %, against a 30 % margin to the boundary. The short and open fault rules are unchanged (0 = disconnected still reads at the raw input). The state names do not change, so no `logic` expression changes.

**If the PMU client cannot divide (CK15).** Two fallbacks, in order: a 2-D table (raw volts × supply volts → state), or fixed windows sized over the whole supply range instead of around one reading - RUN 1153-1470 (11.5-14.8 V), START above 1490. That last one holds only while the key sees 10.4 V or more during a crank, which is what CK14 measures.

**A4 and A5 — ground offsets.** The inhibitor's 8.2 kΩ returns to the engine block (G03); the transit contact's 3.3 kΩ and the 47 kΩ baseline return to the front star (L2-S 1 / 2, G13), which also carries the pop-up motors' current. Both grounds sit *above* the PMU's ground when current flows, never below, so every offset raises a reading. Sensitivities: CRANK_OK moves 103 counts per volt of block offset; TRANSIT+PN 46 per volt of block and 122 per volt of front star; TRANSIT 156 per volt of front star; IDLE 36. With ±20 windows, **CRANK_OK leaves its window at 0.20 V of block offset** - E12 accepts up to 0.5 V battery-negative to block during the crank, which is exactly when `rules crank` reads A4. So a car that passes E12 can chatter its starter on A4 as well. TRANSIT leaves at 0.13 V of front-star offset, while the motors run.

**The fix for A4 and A5: upward windows.** Each state's window runs from (live reading − window) up to the next higher state's lower edge; IDLE runs up to the open threshold. Nothing lands between states but a short or an open. Because an offset only raises a reading, a state can only be misread as the next one up, and that direction is always the refusing one: TRANSIT+PN read as TRANSIT refuses a crank, CRANK_OK read as IDLE refuses a crank, REVERSE read as IDLE drops the reverse lamps. A false P/N is not possible from an offset. Tolerances with upward windows: CRANK_OK 3.9 V of block offset (was 0.20); TRANSIT 1.0 V of front star (was 0.13); TRANSIT+PN 0.74 V of block alone, or 0.28 V of front star alone, or 0.5 V block plus 0.09 V front star together. That last case - cranking in the second a pop-up is moving, on a car at E12's limit - can still refuse the start for that second. It is on the safe side and it is measured (CK14, CK16); if the readings show it matters, the reserve is to move the reference: run the inhibitor's BW return to the dash GND bus instead of the block, one conductor in L1, which is a block for Camden because it moves a wire. A5's REVERSE is read with the engine running, where CK05 expects under 50 mV, so A5 has margin to spare.

**What was not changed.** A1, A2, A6 and A8 return to the dash or the doors, where no load current shares the ground; A3's park contact returns at the wiper motor and was not budgeted here. They keep ± windows.

**In the data.**
- `_schema`: `inputs.decode` is new, enum(window | upward | conductance).
- `inputs`: A15, A16 `conductance`; A4, A5 `upward`; A1, A2, A3, A6, A8 `window`.
- `rules`: `ladder-decode` is new and holds the three methods, the formula and the boundaries.
- `checks`: CK14 (MG23: log A4, A16, the supply and the block offset through a real crank), CK15 (PMU client 5.4: can a function divide, and read the supply voltage), CK16 (MG15 / MG16: log A4, A5 and the front-star offset through a pop-up cycle with the headlamps on).
- `work`: E26's note says how the new windows are entered; R3 done.

title: A surprise takes no PMU channel: an input goes to the ICU and reaches the PMU on CAN, an output shares a PMU channel behind a DCU select as the releases do; V-081's and Q-115's surprises need none
body:
**D-409 — A surprise takes no PMU channel. An input goes to an ICU input and reaches the PMU as a CAN field; a driver's switch goes to the DCU's panel; an output shares an existing PMU channel behind a DCU select, as the releases already do (D-354). The two surprises the risk review named, V-081's pop-up topology and Q-115's speed signal, need no PMU channel at all. Freeing a PMU channel is always his ruling, and the candidates are named with what each costs.** Agent, 2026-09-24, R4 (D-386 risk review). Nobody was asked: this names paths and changes no wire, part or channel.

**The two named surprises.**
- **V-081 / CK08.** If WR turns out to be the pop-up winding's only supply path, the fix is a feed to WR on each side from the same K1 / K2 run feed (or the O1 splice): a conductor per side, not a channel. L2-P is full (4 of 4), so it is a larger housing or a splice at the nose - a wire change, and his block when CK08 says so. Nothing here concludes which topology the motor has (R11).
- **Q-115.** Road speed is an ICU input, IC08 at DP-ICU-B 8 (D-272), not a PMU one. If the B-29 reed switch checks out, it lands on the same IC08 through its pull-up jumper, one conductor into L3-S2 12 or L3-S3; if it does not, the Hall sender already in the design is what is used. The PMU gets speed from 0x200 byte 6 either way.

**The order a surprise takes.**
Inputs:
1. A signal nothing safety-critical gates on → an ICU input and a field in an ICU frame, which the PMU reads as a CAN input. First IC07 at DP-ICU-B 7 (the oil-temperature stage: its carrier stage is built and it sits under a sealing plug until the swap, D-264), then DP-ICU-B 9 (pre-wired to L1-S2 11, D-271; B2's 0-5 V wideband fallback claims it first). Cost: one conductor to the drop and a firmware config row.
2. A switch the driver presses → a key on the DCU's panel (SN19) and a CAN field. Config only.
3. A contact that can join a ladder → a new state on an existing one, one resistor at the switch and the same conductor. Only after the ladder arithmetic says it fits (D-408's decode).
4. A signal the fuel-pump gate, the crank interlock, the brakes or the lamps act on → it must be on a PMU wire, and no input is free. That is a ruling: the only duplicate the PMU has is A7, which the ICU also reads (IC02), and D-260 chose to keep the pump gate off the ICU.

Outputs:
1. A low-current or momentary load → share an existing PMU output with the DCU picking which load, by grounding a relay coil during the PMU's pulse (D-354 / D-370: O10 and K3 / K4). The DCU also has the two low-side switch positions D-329 freed on the comfort carrier (confirm they are still on the board at F11).
2. A comfort-class load → the O15 comfort bus, which carries no load this build, behind the luxury package's own fuses (D-382).
3. **O4 DEFOG** is the one 25 A output doing nothing this build: wired, configured, disabled, no control surface. Taking it forecloses the rear defog until something else carries it - his ruling.
4. **O13 / O14** are capped for the swap; borrowing either forecloses the LS / CD009 swap's ECU or fan feed - his ruling, never a default.
5. A second PMU (the module runs up to five in tandem) - money, his ruling.

**Moving onto CAN to free a channel.** The ICU and DCU duplicate exactly one PMU input, A7 (above). They read no stalk, no ladder and no switch the PMU reads, and the tell-tale senses are ICU inputs on PMU outputs, not PMU channels. So CAN frees nothing for free: every PMU channel is the only reader of its signal, and that is by design - the PMU keeps the car running with both modules dead (recovery, D-322).

**In the data.** `rules spare-capacity` gains the order above as its closing paragraph. R4 done.

title: F3 is split and ignition and the headlamps hold on a ladder fault: the wake stages move to F23, a dead switch feed reads as a fault, ignition drops only on a clean OFF or ACC; the light switch's own feed is block 00.32
body:
**D-410 — F3 is split and ignition and the headlamps hold their state on a ladder fault (block 00.30, option a). The wake stages move to their own 3 A fuse, F23. The key's ladder and the light switch's ladder now read a FAULT, never OFF, when their feed dies with a contact closed. Only a clean OFF or ACC turns ignition off; a FAULT holds it while the engine turns (oil_ok). The headlamps hold their last state while A15 reads a FAULT. The last part, a feed of its own for the light switch, needs a conductor that has no free cavity, and is block 00.32.** Camden, 2026-09-24, in the app.

**His answer.** He chose option (a): "Split F3 into two fuses, and hold state on a fault. One fuse feeds the key switch and the K13 coil; the other feeds the light switch and the wake stages, in a free block-B position or one more sealed inline holder (a few dollars). The PMU logic changes so that only a clean OFF reading turns ignition off (an open or fault reading holds RUN while the engine is turning), and the headlamps hold their last state while A15 reads a fault. Costs one fuse position and logic rows." He typed nothing else.

**What applying it found.** The option assumed the split costs only a fuse position. It needs a conductor too: the ignition switch's B terminal and the light switch's common are both fed by the one conductor L3-S2 2, which branches in the leg behind the column, and the brake-wake plunger (L3-S1 7) branches off it as well. Every cavity in L3-S1 and L3-S2 is used, and the only unused ones in the leg are L3-S3 1-3, the radar pass-throughs held for block 01.11. Where the light switch's own feed runs is where a wire goes, so it is block 00.32, not something decided here. Everything else in (a) is applied now.

**Where the fuses stand.**
- **F3** (5 A, block A pos 2) keeps L3-S2 2: the ignition switch's B terminal, and through it the K13 back-stop coil, the light switch common and the brake-wake plunger until block 00.32 moves the light side.
- **F23** (3 A, sealed inline off the busbar) is new and feeds the wake stages' excitation rail at the dash node, which was the other half of N29. A spare block-B position was not used: block B is fed through K11, which opens when the car sleeps, and the wake stages must be live while it sleeps. N29 now runs F3 to L3-S2 2 only; N87 runs F23 to the wake-stage rail. P002's target goes from 7 to 8 holders.

**How a dead feed reads.** With D-408's decode, a switch whose feed has died still ties the node through its closed contacts to 0 V. That pulls the reading *below* the live OFF reading: by about 20 counts at ACC or PARK, about 44 at RUN or HEAD. With the old ± windows, that sat inside OFF's window, so a blown F3 would have read as the key turned off. Now a reading more than 12 counts below the live OFF reading is a FAULT (supply dead), alongside the open and short rules (`rules ladder-decode`). Confirm at E26: pull F3 with the key at ACC and with the lights at PARK, and read both.

**The logic.**
- **IGNITION:** on at A16 >= RUN. It turns off only after A16 has read a clean OFF or ACC for 200 ms. On an A16 FAULT it holds its state while oil_ok is true, and drops once oil_ok clears. A FAULT never turns it on from off.
  - The PMU has no tach of its own, and D-251 keeps CAN out of these gates. Oil pressure is the PMU's own wire-read sign that the engine is turning.
  - The cost: with the key ladder faulted and the engine running, the key cannot stop the engine. The display says KEY FAULT, and the stop is the master disconnect (recovery RC01), which is what RC01 is for. He chose this.
- **FUEL_PUMP:** its A16 >= RUN terms read the IGNITION channel's own state instead, so the pump holds with the ignition and never outlives it. oil_ok clears when ignition goes off. There is still no CAN term (D-251).
- **HEAD_LOW, HEAD_HIGH, TAIL_PARK:** each holds its last state while A15 reads a FAULT, and annunciates LIGHT SWITCH FAULT. The retry classes do not change.

**In the data.**
- `fuses`: F3 feeds, F23 new.
- `node_conductors`: N29, N87 new.
- `wake_stages`: WS10, WS11, WS16, WS1A, WS20, WS21, WS26, WS2A now say F23.
- `parts`: P002 target and used_for.
- `logic`: IGNITION, FUEL_PUMP, HEAD_LOW, HEAD_HIGH, TAIL_PARK.
- `rules`: ladder-decode (the supply-dead fault).
- `blocks`: 00.30 deleted, 00.32 new.
- `work`: R2 stays open, gated on block 00.32, for the light switch's feed.
